zh:
世上有一种林子，平时看不到。只有雾气最深的夜晚它才长出来。老话说，只有心诚的人才能活着出来。
从前有个痴公子，误打误撞走到这样的林子里。他在雾里走了很久，发现自己一直在打转。他看到了了十几个破庙。那庙很小，看不清供的什么。他身无长物，只好用林中的东西做祭品，给每一座庙都磕头。结果他就糊里糊涂走出了林子。 
当他走出林子，松了一口气的时候，低头一看，却发现自己的影子没了。——他的影子才是真正的祭品，被永远留在了林子里。从此这人就变得疯傻痴呆，最后不知道去哪儿了。
en:
There exists a kind of forest in this world that remains unseen by day. It only grows on nights when the mist is at its thickest. The old tales say that only those with absolute sincerity can walk out of it alive.
Once, a besotted young master stumbled into such a forest. He wandered through the fog for a long time, only to realize he was walking in circles. He came upon a dozen ruined shrines. They were so small he couldn't even tell what was enshrined within. Having nothing of value on him, he used whatever he could find in the dirt as offerings, kowtowing before every single shrine. Somehow, in a daze, he managed to stumble his way out.
When he finally emerged and breathed a sigh of relief, he looked down, only to find his shadow was gone. His shadow was the true offering, left behind in those woods forever. From then on, the man was reduced to a witless husk, and eventually wandered off to who knows where.

zh:
一朝别后，二地空悬。以为三四月，谁知五六年。慰叹终重逢，未料相决绝…… 
白微，师尊常言，“一命一价”。洪水将袭、绣金逼迫，至此绝境，吾方悟此言。
出逃，则敌夺手札、毒患复起；固守，则全城无虞，然我等十死无生。
我据实相告，拜而请。默然良久后，友人苏茂慨叹曰：“愿随之。为小妹、为亲友，以死换生。”余者或悲或泣，然终纷纷留守。
见状，我心慰藉，又生遗憾。然一命一价，为护珍爱之人，为保天下安宁，愿以我等性命为价。

白微，愿有一日，你得见此信，知我憾恨与无奈。愿有一日，你得见手札，传之当传之人，以此为助，根除毒患。
白微，愿你无病无恙，一世长安。
en:
Ever since we parted years ago, there's been an emptiness in my heart. I thought we might find solace in each other when we finally met someday—never expecting that day would never come.
Our master often said, "One life, one price." Unfortunately, now with the flood looming and Aureate Pavilion closing in, I finally understand the weight behind his words.
If we fled, the enemy would seize our journals and the poison would rise anew. If we stayed, the city would be safe—yet at the cost of our lives.
So, I asked them for their opinions. Despite great grief, they all chose to stay, for their beloved ones. As you can see, one life, one price. For the sake of those we hold dear, for the peace of the world, we offer our own lives as the price.

I hope that one day you find this letter and understand my regret and desperation behind it. I hope you find the journal as well—pass it to the right hands to end this plague forever.
May you live in health and peace all your days.

显德五年三月十四日
立分书单人 周齐岩（押） 周齐石（押） 周齐磊（押） 周齐砀（押）
en:
Property Division Contract of the Zhou Family, Mercyheart Town, Qinghe

We, Zhou Qiyan, along with younger brothers Qishi, Qilei, and Qidang, hereby establish this contract. Our ancestor, Master Zihui, was a skilled stone carver who braved hardships to establish our family business, accumulating considerable wealth. From the sixth year of Kaiyuan to the present day, our craft has been passed down faithfully through sixteen generations without neglect. Yet since the Emperor's ban on Buddhism three years ago, our trade has withered. No work means no food. To secure our livelihoods, we divide all assets to save the single house reserved for our father, Xiuli, in his retirement, into monetary shares. The total value of stone materials, houses, fields, and tools amounts to 176 strings of cash, divided equally into four portions. Zhou Qiyan receives the single house and 26 strings; Zhou Qishi receives 50 strings; Zhou Qilei receives 50 strings; Zhou Qidang receives 50 strings. From this day forth, each shall hold their share without dispute. Should any violate this agreement, the offending party shall be reported to the authorities, and this document shall serve as binding proof. Four identical copies are made, marked Heaven, Earth, Man, and Harmony for each party to keep in perpetuity.

14th Day of the Third Month, Fifth Year of the Xiande Era

Signatories:
Zhou Qiyan (seal)
Zhou Qishi (seal)
Zhou Qilei (seal)
Zhou Qidang (seal)

en: The name "Broken Bridge" dates back to the Tang Dynasty, immortalized in Bai Juyi's verse, which lamented its desolate, moss-covered state. In his day, the bridge was likely smothered in wild growth; today, it is veiled by weeping willows, the long causeway draped across the water like a trailing silk ribbon. The landscape has transformed entirely. When the winter snows finally melt, the white frost atop the bridge's arch melts first, while the causeway banks remain heavily blanketed. From a distance, the snowline appears abruptly severed, earning the beloved title, "Lingering Snow on the Broken Bridge." Since antiquity, this has been the lake's most bustling crossing. I only fear that one day, buckling beneath the endless crowds, the bridge may finally live up to its name.

zh:
石头这个名字，是石老大给取的。那时石老大还不是老大，石头也还只是一颗圆滚滚的小石子儿。

太阳是个很准时的家伙。每天它一冒头，石头就陪着石老大去那个黑乎乎的洞口。
等太阳回家睡觉了，石头就会蹲在老地方，等那个熟悉的身影走出来。然后一人一狗，踩着夕阳的余晖，慢慢走回屋子睡觉。

可今天，天都黑透了，石老大还没出来。

石头慌了。它不懂什么叫塌方，它只知道，老大不见了。
它开始狂吠，汪汪汪！汪汪汪！！
石头的叫声喊来了许多人，不多久，老大也被人扶了出来。

大家都夸多亏了石头，还好石头在。

矿石无心，还好石头有心。
en:
Stone got his name from Big Brother Shi. Back then, Shi wasn't a Big Brother yet, and Stone was just a round little pebble.

The sun was punctual. Every day it rose, and Stone followed Big Brother Shi to that dark hole in the mountain.
When the sun went home to sleep, Stone waited in the same spot, watching for the familiar figure to emerge. Then, one dog, one man, walking home in twilight.

But today, darkness fell. Big Brother didn't come out.

Stone panicked. He didn't know the word collapse. He only knew: Big Brother Shi was gone.
He started barking. WOOF WOOF WOOF! WOOF WOOF WOOF!!
The barking brought people. Soon, Big Brother Shi was carried out.

Everyone praised Stone. Good thing Stone was there.

The ores may be cold and heartless, but Stone has a heart of gold.

zh: 薛丑在开封的交引铺里见到了王十三。他有些好奇，不知道为什么这个女娃娃的眼神中，透着一股狼一般的狠劲。老板则告诉薛丑，这娃娃是自己在街边捡到的，不知来历，但在做生意上是一把好手。薛丑留了心眼，他来交引铺谈了几回生意，最后一回来时，他问王十三，要不要跟他离开。王十三回头望了眼那家小小的交引铺，她清楚地知道，交引铺只是自己一时的停靠地，在这儿她得不到自己想要的。而薛丑背后，是未知，也是希望。她没有拒绝。王十三就这样跟着薛丑进了九流门。薛丑看中王十三的玲珑心，将她放在自己身边，常与她合计九流门的事宜。他们都不信人心，但是信利益。薛丑需要王十三，王十三则需要九流门背后的情报网。虽然九流门也未必是她的最后归属，但在这个当下，王十三需要这样一个地方。当双方有利益纠葛时，盟友的关系是最坚固的。而等九流门的情势稳定后，薛丑在鬼市子经营起官财坊的生意，王十三则在官财坊开了一家当铺。十一当铺有自己的一套规矩，在江湖上掀起了不小的风浪。王十三便游走于这些有所图谋的人之间，处处布下她的棋局。她是九流门背后的最强支撑。但不久，官财坊发生凶杀案，官财坊关停，当铺的生意也受了影响。王十三便整日在鬼街游荡。但她是个闲不住的人，索性在鬼街边摆起了棋摊。她那颗七窍玲珑心，可透过棋局，看进人的心里去。这来鬼街的客人是人是鬼，一盘棋，便能叫她看的分明。
en: Xue Chou first encountered Wang Shisan at the banknote exchange in Kaifeng. He had been curious. What kind of story lay behind the wolf-like gleam in this young girl's eyes? The shopkeeper told him she'd been taken in off the streets, her background a blank slate, but she had an uncanny head for business. Intrigued, Xue Chou returned a few more times under the guise of work. On his final visit, he asked her if she would leave with him. Wang Shisan turned to glance at the humble exchange house behind her. She had always known this place was merely a stepping stone; she couldn't get what she wanted here. And behind Xue Chou lay the unknown and the possibility of everything. So she went with him, stepping into the Nine Mortal Ways. Recognizing her shrewdness, Xue Chou keeps her close, seeking her counsel on many matters within the sect. They are not bound by trust in each other, only by a shared trust in mutual interest. He needs her insight; she needs the information network that comes with the sect. It might not be her final destination, but at that moment, it is the right place to be. And when two people want something from each other, their alliance is ironclad. After the sect found its footing, Xue Chou opened a public Fortune Beyond Parlor in the Ghostlight Market, while Wang Shisan established her own pawnshop in the market, Eleven Pawn, which operated under its own strict set of rules, quickly stirring a buzz across the jianghu. Wang Shisan weaved her way through the schemes of others, setting up her own trick at every turn. Behind the rise of the Nine Mortal Ways, she was the sharpest mind. But the peace didn't last. A murder took place inside the public Fortune Beyond Parlor, forcing it to shut down, and Eleven Pawn soon suffered from the fallout. Wang Shisan wandered Ghost Street with nothing to do, but idleness didn't suit her. So she set up a chess stall at the far edge of the street. With her mind as sharp as ever, she read her visitors move by move—whether they came as men or as monsters, one game of chess was all it took for her to see them for what they truly were.

zh:
西湖东岸，清波门外。杏林陈氏，世居钱塘。一道门庭隔开市声，内里幽径回环，花影掩映垂柳，半湖山色尽揽入怀。当家者，「玉山君」陈子奚；爱徒「观音针」陈慎为少主。宅中大小事务由总管安叔操持。玉山君医名满江湖，门前却少见车马。
有一桩雅事，杭人津津乐道：逢月明之夜，常见玉山君自陈宅出湖，独棹一舟，载酒入湖，行至水心，自斟自酌，醉则倚棹而眠，任孤舟随波。夜渔的、晚游的，行船与他擦肩，相视笑说神仙中人，不过如此。久之相传，唤作「玉山泛月」。
玉山君好酒，正如太白所咏：「鸬鹚杓，鹦鹉杯。百年三万六千日，一日须倾三百杯。」只是世人多羡风流，少有人问：一人独饮这许多酒，是贪杯，还是浇愁？那愁又有几多，竟要倾尽如许杯盏？较之盏中春醪孰深孰浅；较之西湖水又如何？
en:
On the eastern shore of West Lake, beyond Qingbo Gate, the Chen family of physicians have lived in Qiantang for generations. A single gate separates the household from the clamor of the streets; within, paths wind between willows and flowers, and half the lake and hills come with the view. The head of the house is Chen Zixi, known as Mister Jade Hill; his favored student Chen Shen, known as Guanyin Needle, is heir. Uncle An the steward sees to all household affairs. Mister Jade Hill is a famed physician, yet few carriages come to his door.
The people of Hangzhou love to tell one story about him: On bright nights he takes a boat out alone, rows to the middle of the lake, and drinks by himself, until he falls asleep against the oar and lets the boat go where it will. Night fishermen and late boaters pass him, look at each other, and say that is what an immortal looks like. They call the sight Jade Hill by the Moon.
Mister Jade Hill loves his wine, like Li Bai once sang: "Cormorant ladle, parrot cup, thirty-six thousand days in a life and three hundred cups on each of them." People admire his style, but few ask why he drinks that much wine alone. Does he drink for joy, or to drown a sorrow? And how deep must that sorrow be, to need so many cups? Deeper than the cup of wine? Or deeper than the West Lake itself?

zh:
上官闲从前不叫这名。
他爹给他取名上官赢，打小请了先生教棋，指望他赢遍天下，光宗耀祖。
他也争气，十来岁就把县里的老棋手杀得片甲不留。
人人都说这孩子是棋呆子，除了下棋，旁的什么都不上心。
后来他去了开封，想赢更大的。
他在棋摊子上坐了一天一夜，连赢了十七盘。第十八盘的时候，碰到了个老头。
老头胡子拉碴，穿得破破烂烂，也不说话，落子慢吞吞的，像没睡醒。
上官赢以为自己稳赢，结果中盘被老头一个飞刀，杀得满盘皆输。
他不服，又下一盘，又输。再下一盘，还是输。
老头收了棋子，拍拍膝盖站起来，说了一句：“你太想赢了。”
上官赢愣在那里。他想说下棋不就是为了赢吗？可话到嘴边，突然觉得没意思了。
后来他把名字改了，叫上官闲。棋还是下，但不再争输赢。走哪儿算哪儿，吃哪儿住哪儿。
走到乐安浦的时候，闻见一阵鲜鱼汤的香味，脚就走不动了。
他在村口铺了个草席，喝完鲜鱼汤又吃肉丸子，吃完肉丸子又捧着坛子喝酒。
吃饱了，就往树底下一坐，掏出棋盘，朝路过的人招手：“来，杀一盘？”
不管输赢，他都笑呵呵的，还夸别人棋艺好。
大家说他是个怪人，他装作没听见似的。
“怪就怪呗，又不耽误吃饭。”
en:
Shangguan Xian wasn't always called by that name.
At birth, his father named him Shangguan Ying. Ying was for "Victory." From the time he was a boy, tutors were hired with a single, heavy expectation: he would conquer the chess world and bring glory to their bloodline.
For a long time, he lived up to it. By his early teens, he was slaughtering the county's veteran players, sweeping the board without breaking a sweat. People called him a chess savant, a boy who cared for absolutely nothing beyond the chessboard.
But the county was small, and his ambition was vast. So, he traveled to the great capital of Kaifeng, looking for bigger prey.
He set up at a street-side chess stall and played for a day and a night, racking up seventeen straight wins. Then came the eighteenth match. His opponent was an old man.
The man was unkempt, dressed in rags with a scruffy, untamed beard. He didn't speak. He moved his pieces at a sluggish, lethargic pace, looking half-asleep. Ying thought it would be an effortless slaughter. But mid-game, the old man slipped in a move as sharp and sudden as a hidden blade, shattering Ying's entire strategy in a single breath.
Unwilling to concede, Ying demanded a rematch. He lost. He demanded a third. He lost again.
The old man slowly collected his pieces, dusted off his knees, and stood. "You want to win too badly," he said softly.
Shangguan Ying froze. He opened his mouth to argue. Wasn't winning the whole point of the game? But the words died in his throat. A sudden, crushing exhaustion washed over him.
He changed his name not long after. He became Shangguan Xian. Xian was for "Leisure." He still played, but the ruthless hunger for dominance was gone. He turned into a drifter, going wherever the wind blew, eating whatever he crossed paths with, and sleeping wherever the sun went down.
When his wandering brought him to Tranquil Pier, the rich, savory aroma of fresh fish broth caught on the breeze, and his feet simply refused to take another step.
He rolled out a straw mat right at the edge of the village. He drank his fill of the soup, polished off a bowl of meatballs, and then sat back, happily cradling a jug of wine.
Belly full and perfectly content, he settled into the shade of a large tree, set up his board, and waved at anyone passing by. "Come on!" he'd call out cheerfully. "Care for a match?"
Win or lose, he just laughed a warm, booming laugh, quick to praise a clever move from his opponent.
The villagers whispered that he was an eccentric, a strange vagabond. He acted as if he didn't hear a word of it.
"So I'm a little strange," he'd muse with a smile. "It certainly doesn't ruin my appetite."

zh:
【雅·小雅】

鹿鸣之什

鹿鸣

呦呦鹿鸣，食野之苹。我有嘉宾，鼓瑟吹笙。吹笙鼓簧，承筐是将。人之好我，示我周行。
呦呦鹿鸣，食野之蒿。我有嘉宾，德音孔昭。视民不恌，君子是则是效。我有旨酒，嘉宾式燕以敖。
呦呦鹿鸣，食野之芩。我有嘉宾，鼓瑟鼓琴。鼓瑟鼓琴，和乐且湛。我有旨酒，以燕乐嘉宾之心。

四牡

四牡騑騑，周道倭迟。岂不怀归？王事靡盬，我心伤悲。
四牡騑騑，啴啴骆马。岂不怀归？王事靡盬，不遑启处。
翩翩者鵻，载飞载下，集于苞栩。王事靡盬，不遑将父。
翩翩者鵻，载飞载止，集于苞杞。王事靡盬，不遑将母。
驾彼四骆，载骤骎骎。岂不怀归？是用作歌，将母来谂。
……
南有嘉鱼之什

南有嘉鱼

南有嘉鱼，烝然罩罩。君子有酒，嘉宾式燕以乐。
南有嘉鱼，烝然汕汕。君子有酒，嘉宾式燕以衎。
南有樛木，甘瓠累之。君子有酒，嘉宾式燕绥之。
翩翩者鵻，烝然来思。君子有酒，嘉宾式燕又思。
……

鸿雁之什

鸿雁

鸿雁于飞，肃肃其羽。之子于征，劬劳于野。爰及矜人，哀此鳏寡。
鸿雁于飞，集于中泽。之子于垣，百堵皆作。虽则劬劳，其究安宅？
鸿雁于飞，哀鸣嗷嗷。维此哲人，谓我劬劳。维彼愚人，谓我宣骄。
……

节南山之什

节南山

节彼南山，维石岩岩。赫赫师尹，民具尔瞻。忧心如惔，不敢戏谈。国既卒斩，何用不监！
节彼南山，有实其猗。赫赫师尹，不平谓何。天方荐瘥，丧乱弘多。民言无嘉，憯莫惩嗟。
尹氏大师，维周之氐；秉国之钧，四方是维。天子是毗，俾民不迷。不吊昊天，不宜空我师。
弗躬弗亲，庶民弗信。弗问弗仕，勿罔君子。式夷式已，无小人殆。琐琐姻亚，则无膴仕。
昊天不佣，降此鞠訩。昊天不惠，降此大戾。君子如届，俾民心阕。君子如夷，恶怒是违。
不吊昊天，乱靡有定。式月斯生，俾民不宁。忧心如酲，谁秉国成？不自为政，卒劳百姓。
驾彼四牡，四牡项领。我瞻四方，蹙蹙靡所骋。
方茂尔恶，相尔矛矣。既夷既怿，如相酬矣。
昊天不平，我王不宁。不惩其心，覆怨其正。

谷风之什

谷风

习习谷风，维风及雨。将恐将惧，维予与女。将安将乐，女转弃予。
习习谷风，维风及颓。将恐将惧，置予于怀。将安将乐，弃予如遗。
习习谷风，维山崔嵬。无草不死，无木不萎。忘我大德，思我小怨。
……

甫田之什

甫田

倬彼甫田，岁取十千。我取其陈，食我农人。自古有年。今适南亩，或耘或耔。黍稷薿薿，攸介攸止，烝我髦士。
以我齐明，与我牺羊，以社以方。我田既臧，农夫之庆。琴瑟击鼓，以御田祖。以祈甘雨，以介我稷黍，以穀我士女。
曾孙来止，以其妇子。馌彼南亩，田畯至喜。攘其左右，尝其旨否。禾易长亩，终善且有。曾孙不怒，农夫克敏。
曾孙之稼，如茨如梁。曾孙之庾，如坻如京。乃求千斯仓，乃求万斯箱。黍稷稻粱，农夫之庆。报以介福，万寿无疆。
……

鱼藻之什

鱼藻

鱼在在藻，有颁其首。王在在镐，岂乐饮酒。
鱼在在藻，有莘其尾。王在在镐，饮酒乐岂。
鱼在在藻，依于其蒲。王在在镐，有那其居。
……
en:
【Ya - Minor Odes】 Deer Cry Deer Cry Deer cry, "yow, yow," as they feed on the wild southernwood. I have here admirable guests; the lutes are struck, the organ blows. The organ blows till all its tongues are moving. The baskets of offerings are presented to them. The men love me, and will show me the perfect path. Deer cry, "yow, yow," as they feed on the wild southernwood. I have here admirable guests, whose fame is grandly bright. They show the people not to be mean; the officers have in them a pattern and model. I have good wine, which my admirable guests drink, enjoying themselves. Deer cry, "yow, yow," as they feed on the wild southernwood. I have here admirable guests; the lutes are struck, the organs played. The lutes are struck, the organs played till their tongues blend in harmony. I have good wine, with which to gladden the hearts of my admirable guests. Four Steeds My four steeds are ever toiling; the great way stretches far before them. Am I not anxious to return? But the king's business must not be slackly discharged; and my heart is wounded with sadness. My four steeds are ever toiling; the black-maned white steeds are all in a lather. Am I not anxious to return? But the king's business must not be slackly discharged; and I have not leisure to kneel or sit. Now flit the doves, now up, now down, and settle on the bushy oaks. The king's business must not be slackly discharged; and I have not leisure to nourish my father. Now flit the doves, now up, now down, and settle on the bushy medlars. The king's business must not be slackly discharged; and I have not leisure to nourish my mother. I yoked my four white steeds, and they hurried on, eager to be gone. Am I not anxious to return? [But] I make this song, to tell of my mother's tender care. ... Fine Fish in the South Fine Fish in the South In the south are fine fish, swimming about, now below, now above. The prince has spirits; and his admirable guests will feast, and be happy. In the south are fine fish, swimming about, now to the left, now to the right. The prince has spirits; and his admirable guests will feast, and enjoy themselves. In the south are the drooping trees, and the gourds clinging to them. The prince has spirits; and his admirable guests will feast, and be at ease. Now flit the doves, flocking together. The prince has spirits; and his admirable guests will feast, and be happy. ... Wild Geese Wild Geese The wild geese are flying about; - Sorrowfully are they moving their wings. The travellers are on their way; - Toilsome are their exertions in the wilds. Pity the helpless and solitary; - Alas for the forlorn and the widowed! The wild geese are flying about; - They settle in the middle of the marsh. The travellers are raising the walls; - A hundred cubits are all completed. Though they toil thus, - Where will they dwell at last? The wild geese are flying about; - Mournfully they cry. Those intelligent men say that we are toiling; - But the foolish think that we are showing off our pride. ... Lofty South Hill Lofty South Hill Lofty is that southern hill, with its rugged masses of rocks! Awe-inspiring are you, O [Grand-]Master Yin, and the people all look to you! Their hearts are as if on fire; they dare not speak of you in jest. The kingdom is verging to extinction; - How is it that you do not consider this? Lofty is that southern hill, and very rugged are its rocks! Awe-inspiring are you, O [Grand-]Master Yin, but how is it that you are so unjust? Heaven is sending down death and disorder, and destruction and famine is prevailing. The people have nothing good to say of you; - Yet you do not correct, nor bemoan yourself. O Yin, the Grand-Master, you are the stay of Zhou; you grasp the power of the kingdom, and maintain it on every side. You assist the Son of Heaven, so that the people are not deceived. O unpitying great Heaven, it is not right that you should thus send down ruin on us all. He does not himself attend to the government, and the people have no confidence in him. He makes no inquiry about them, and no trial of their services; he should not deal deceitfully with superior men. If he would dismiss them, and put a stop [to their employment], there would be no discontent among the people. O ye of trivial services, you should not hold offices of importance. O unpitying great Heaven, there is no end to the disorder! With every month it continues to grow, so that the people have no repose. I am as if intoxicated with the grief of my heart. Who holds the ordering of the kingdom? He does not attend to the government himself, and the result is toil and suffering to the people. I yoke my four steeds, my four steeds, long-necked. I look to the four quarters; distress is everywhere; there is no place I can drive to. When your evil is thus violent, you look to your spears. When you are pleased and appeased, you lay them aside again. O great Heaven, unjust, our king does not rest. He will not correct his heart, but goes on to resent endeavours to rectify him. I, Jiafu, make this song, to lay bare the king's disorders. If you would but change your heart, and nourish the myriad regions! ... Valley Wind Valley Wind Gently blows the east wind, with cloudy skies and rain. In the time of peril, of dread, it was I alone that you kept. Now, in the time of repose and happiness, you turn and cast me away. Gently blows the east wind, and the clouds are piled up. In the time of peril, of dread, you placed me in your bosom. Now, in the time of repose and happiness, you cast me away as a thing abandoned.

Gently blows the east wind, and the hills are covered with clouds. There is no grass which does not die, no tree which does not wither. You forget my great virtues, and think of the small grudges I cherish. ... Large Field Large Field Large is that field, and the yearly produce from it is ten thousand measures. I take its old stores, and give them to our husbandmen, for the nourishment of our guests. From of old we have had good years. I now go to the south-lying acres, where some are weeding, some are covering up the roots. The millets look luxuriant; and the spirits are presented, and the victims offered, to seek for blessings. With my vessels full of bright millet, and my pure victims, we sacrifice to the spirits of the land, and to those of the four quarters. My fields being in good order, my husbandmen are encouraged. With lutes, and with drums, we invoke the Father of Husbandry, to pray for sweet rain, to increase the produce of our millets, and to bless my men and women. The descendant comes, with his wife and children, bringing food to those south-lying acres. The surveyor of the fields comes and is glad. He takes of the right and the left, and tastes whether the food is good or not. The grain is abundant, and the fields are well cultivated. The descendant is not angry; his husbandmen are encouraged. The grain of the descendant, piled up, looks like a wall, like a hill. He prepares a thousand granaries; he makes ten thousand carts. The millet, the rice, and the glutinous millet are abundant; and the husbandmen receive praise. May the spirits reward you with great happiness, with long life endless! ... Fish in the Pond Fish in the Pond The fish are in the pond; large are their heads. The king is in Hao, drinking, and happy. The fish are in the pond; long are their tails. The king is in Hao, drinking, and happy. The fish are in the pond; they rest in the mud. The king is in Hao; his dwelling is pleasant. ...

听一书生说他去某某客栈投宿，半夜偷看隔壁，见一光头和尚搂着妇人。次日告与店家，店家笑说是东家娘子，素来信佛，请高僧来讲经的。

听说春香楼老鸨周某，近日被人半夜戳中心口，人当场死了，本来她就经常克扣手下妓女的赎身钱，这下都没人给她下葬。
听说某某地有三人都亲耳听到李财主家的骡子，忽然开口说了句人话，自言“今年收成不好”。请道士来做法，道士说骡子活不过三日。果然第三天骡子倒地死了。
听说北边道上出了个怪人，专抢过路商贩的鞋子。不抢银子不抢货，只把两只鞋子扒走，留下光脚。有个被抢的商人骂了句晦气，第二天就摔断了腿。有人说是山精作怪，也有人说是个疯乞丐。
听说曲城南王阿婆卖菜，少给了客几两，被人发现之后，王阿婆当街谩骂起来，正巧一姓澹台的捕快路过撞见。捕快说“欺诈骗秤，又口出恶言”，当场就要剪了那王阿婆的舌头。众人跪了一地求情，最后判她自扇五十个耳光，王阿婆吓得半个月没敢出门。
en:
In business, nothing matters more than sharp eyes and keen ears. These are notes gathered from my travels, sure to prove useful someday!

I heard that Squire Wang Fu of a village in Hedong, nearly sixty years old, recently took an eighteen-year-old concubine. Half a month later, she ran off with the accountant and all his gold and silver, leaving Squire Wang bedridden with rage.
Old Matriarch Sun of Shanyang City said the fourth son of her master's household had his leg broken, and his brothers are plotting to cast him out.
A scholar claimed that while lodging at an inn, he peeked into the next room at midnight and saw a bald monk embracing a woman. When he reported it the next morning, the innkeeper laughed and explained it was the mistress of the house, a devout Buddhist who had invited the monk to explain the sutras.
Liu San the woodcutter said Widow Zhao at the West City Tofu Shop has skin so fair she is called the Tofu Belle. The fourth son of the Sun Silk Shop visits her shop daily, lingering in the kitchen for half an hour each time.
I heard Madam Zhou of Fragrance Pavilion was stabbed through the heart at midnight and died instantly. Having constantly skimmed the redemption funds of her courtesans, she now has no one willing to bury her.
Three people in a nearby town swore they heard Landlord Li's mule speak in human tongue, muttering, "The harvest will be poor this year." A Daoist priest was hired to perform a ritual and predicted the beast would not live three days. Sure enough, it dropped dead on the third day.
Word is that a bizarre rogue appeared on the northern road, robbing passing merchants of nothing but their shoes. Leaving them barefoot without taking a single coin or scrap of cargo. One merchant cursed his luck and broke his leg the very next day. Some claim it is a mountain spirit at work, while others say it is just a mad beggar.
Granny Wang in southern Qucheng was caught shortchanging vegetable weights and hurled vile curses in the street, only to run into a constable surnamed Tantai. Declaring her guilty of "deceitful weights and foul speech," the constable moved to slit her tongue on the spot. The crowd knelt to plead for her, and she was ultimately sentenced to slap herself fifty times, leaving her too terrified to step outside for half a month.
Recently, while resting at an inn, a bystander noticed a man and woman exchanging flirtatious glances, clearly up to no good. The same bystander approached to chat, but they ignored him. Hah! One glance told the bystander that the woman was no respectable lady, and the man was utterly bewitched. Righteous indignation stirred within him: he first deceived the woman, hinting that the man had already spilled her past to others and was merely using her; then he turned to warn the man that she was running a badger game and would leave him penniless, making sure to lay bare the truth about Fragrance Pavilion. In less than half a day, the pair had parted ways, their futures saved by that bystander.
And who was that bystander? Why, kindhearted me, of course.

zh:
阿郎一天一天长大。从小自由生长的他，却没有成为粗鄙的野孩子。
有足够的自由，孩子便没有什么叛逆的心思。——因为想要做的事情，只要不伤风败俗作奸犯科，阿娘都会鼓励他去尝试。
若是成了，娘儿两个一起欢呼雀跃，若是不成，万雁的宽慰便会拂去孩子心头的阴霾。
反正阿娘都在，也没什么好怕的。
阿郎很小就知道什么该做，什么不该做，什么喜欢，什么不喜欢。

一天，阿郎放学回来抱回来一个硕大的棋盘。
“阿娘，这是嫖姚棋。”阿郎兴冲冲地向万雁解释。
“快给阿娘看看。”万雁习惯地接过来。可这一次，阿郎轻巧地避开了万雁的手。
“这是……学堂朋友的，我们别碰坏了。”阿郎顿了顿，放下褡裢。“娘，我和朋友出去玩了，晚饭莫等我。”
看着阿郎出门的背影，万雁终于发现，阿郎已经长这么高了。

她当然喜欢孩子有自己的朋友，也喜欢孩子去体验各种新奇有趣的东西。
她没有怪孩子。她知道，自己终究该放手了。
想陪孩子更久，她就要努力去理解孩子的世界。
“瓢……舀棋？什么名字。”万雁自嘲地笑笑。
明天，我也去集市上，买一个回来玩吧。
en:
A'Lang grew day by day. Having grown up freely, he did not become a crude wild child. 
With enough freedom, a child harbors little rebellion—because anything he wanted to try, as long as it wasn't immoral or illegal, his mother encouraged him to do. 
If he succeeded, mother and son would rejoice together. If he failed, Wan Yan's comfort would brush away the gloom from the child's heart. 
After all, Mother was always there. Nothing to fear. 
From a young age, A'Lang knew what should be done, what shouldn't, what he liked, and what he didn't. 

One day, A'Lang came home from school carrying a large game board. 
"Mom, this is Piaoyao Battleboard," A'Lang excitedly explained to Wan Yan. 
"Let Mom see." Wan Yan habitually reached for it. But this time, A'Lang deftly avoided her hand. 
"This is... a friend's from school. We shouldn't damage it." A'Lang paused, putting down his bag. "Mom, I'm going out with friends. Don't wait for me for dinner." 
Watching A'Lang's back as he left, Wan Yan finally realized how tall her son had grown. 

Of course, she was glad her child had friends, glad he was experiencing new and interesting things. 
She didn't blame him. She knew, eventually, she had to let go. 
If she wanted to be with her child longer, she had to try to understand his world. 
"Swash... barkler? What a name." Wan Yan smiled self-deprecatingly. 
Tomorrow, I'll go to the market and buy one to try.

zh: 舂捣，造纸之工序也。蒸料既熟，置石臼中力舂之，使纤维细碎如泥，古谓之“捣纸”。其用在水力臼中反复舂之，使纤维分散，沉浮于浆。纤维愈细，纸质愈匀，故舂捣之工，不可草率。
en: Historically known as "pounding paper" (Daozhi), pulp beating crushes the cooked fibers into a workable paste. The softened raw materials are placed in a stone mortar and pounded relentlessly, often with the aid of water-powered trip hammers, until reduced to a fine mash. This thorough beating disperses the fibers evenly so they suspend properly in water. Because the smoothness of the finished paper depends on how thoroughly the pulp is crushed, this process demands meticulous care.

zh:
选手须遵守《燕云十六声》通用赛事规则，详见燕云十六声赛事中心官网【通用赛事规则】一栏。

比赛中游侠的部分战斗属性会进行调平（心法为6重，奇术为6重9段，解锁当前赛季所有通用型止戈天赋），战斗规则与「论剑」玩法中的规则相同。

海选初赛开放时间内报名参赛的游侠需要自行前往论剑赛海选界面参与匹配，完成10场海选比赛，胜利4场即可晋级海选复赛。
海选复赛开放时间内，晋级复赛的游侠需要自行前往论剑赛海选界面参与匹配，完成15场海选比赛，排名前64名的游侠晋级下一阶段比赛。
参赛选手将根据胜场进行排名，胜场较高的选手排名靠前，若胜场相同则比较胜场平均用时胜场平均用时较短的选手排名靠前。

小组循环赛比赛开始前15分钟参赛选手可进入准备场景，赛制为单循环积分赛，采用三局两胜制。
【1】匹配机制：系统将于14:00开始自动为各战队匹配未对阵过的对手，
【2】匹配流程：每次返回准备场景后，系统会持续进行新一轮匹配，由于仅匹配未交战的对手，可能出现等待时间较长的情况，请耐心等待。
【3】单循环赛制：需与小组内所有选手完成一轮对阵，小组赛将在所有参赛选手完成相互对阵后结束。
审核时间结束后各小组第一名晋级八强胜者组、第二名晋级八强败者组，奖励在审核期结束后领取。

排名规则（优先级）：
参赛选手将根据胜场进行排名，胜场较高的选手排名靠前；若胜场相同则比较净胜分（净胜分=所有小场胜场-所有小场负场），净胜分较高的选手排名靠前；若净胜分相同，则将对比双方的胜负关系。
若出现三名或以上选手胜场数与净胜分均相同，则仅计算这些选手之间的相互比赛结果，再按照上述规则依次比较，若仍无法区分，则比较小循环内胜利用时，用时较短的一方排名靠前。
en:
Players must abide by the Where Winds Meet General Tournament Rules. See the [General Tournament Rules] section on the official Where Winds Meet Tournament Center website. 

Combat attributes will be balanced during the match (Inner Ways Tier 6, Mystic Skill Tier 6 Stage 9,  all current season general Arena Talents unlocked). Combat rules follow the 1v1 Arena rules. 

Wanderers registered during the Initial Qualifiers period must proceed to the 1v1 Arena Tournament Qualifiers interface to match. Complete 10 qualifying matches; 4 wins are required to advance to the Secondary Qualifiers. 

During the Secondary Qualifiers, advancing Wanderers must proceed to the 1v1 Arena Tournament Qualifiers interface to match. Complete 15 qualifying matches. The top 64 Wanderers advance to the next stage. 

Participants are ranked by wins. Higher wins rank higher. If wins are equal, compare average time per win; shorter average time ranks higher.

Participating players can enter the preparation scene 15 minutes before the Group Round Robin match starts. The format is a Single Round Robin tournament, using a Best of 3 format. 
[1] Matchmaking: The system will automatically match players against opponents they haven't fought yet starting at 14:00. 
[2] Process: After returning to the preparation scene, the system will continue to match for the next round. Wait times may be longer as it only matches opponents not yet fought. Please wait patiently. 
[3] Round Robin: Players must complete a match against every other player in the group. The Group Stage ends when all participating players have fought each other. 
After the review time ends, the 1st place of each group advances to the Top 8 Winners Bracket, and the 2nd place advances to the Top 8 Losers Bracket. Rewards are claimed after the review period. 

Ranking Rules (Priority):
Participants are ranked by wins (higher is better). If wins are equal, compare Net Score (Net Score = Total Game Wins - Total Game Losses); higher Net Score ranks higher. If Net Score is equal, compare the Head-to-Head result.

If three or more players have equal wins and Net Scores, calculate results only among these players using the rules above. If still indistinguishable, compare time taken for wins in the small cycle; shorter time ranks higher.

Outside the little hut at Homeward Wilds, several Inkbound Order disciples are in the middle of a lively debate over the origins of the stone lions. One is certain they once stood along the spirit way of an imperial tomb; another insists they are merely an artisan's flourish, nothing more than a display of skill; a third is convinced that some long-lost treasure must lie hidden beneath them. The moment they spot you, they crowd around at once, chattering over one another to offer their theories and ask what you think...

At your answer, the disciples fall briefly silent and trade bewildered glances. They scratch their heads, and after a long pause, someone ventures that this place used to be nothing but wilderness, so perhaps the sudden appearance of the stone lions is due to some strange stirring in the earth's veins; another still refuses to yield, insisting there must be an imperial tomb here, with the lions marking the way... With no one quite able to follow your meaning, you can only let out a wry, inward smile. Turning back, you look once more at the largest stone lion. It still stands there quietly as ever, head lifted proudly into the wind, immovable, timeless, unchanged through the ages.

蟹黄本不是藏书馆的小狗，是学子们外出赶海时捡回来的。
蟹黄被发现时才巴掌大，正与滩涂上的大鳌蟹斗得激烈。众人怜它勇武，便将它带回藏书馆，养在膳堂里。
有了蟹黄，膳堂里的夜磨子便无所遁形。偶尔有溜进膳堂寻吃食的学子，也被蟹黄吠得连连退却。
承蒙膳堂师父学子投喂，蟹黄的胃口越发刁钻。不食脏污之饭，不食掌上之物。非要用盆碗盛了端在眼前，它才会趴下前爪，似是行礼道谢，随后才开始享用。
众人皆说，蟹黄入学后懂了礼，是书院的好狗狗。蟹黄听不懂，只是摇着尾巴。
日子就像盆里的饭菜，冒尖又见底。如今蟹黄也老了，它便也不再巡视着膳堂。
它常趴在花树下，眯着眼。
紫英缤纷，它好像又变成了当年泥泞里勇敢的小狗，不怕蟹螯，不怕浪头。
en:
Roe had not always been a dog of the Archives. It was found by students during one of their outings of seaside foraging and brought back with them.
When discovered, Roe was no bigger than a palm, locked in fierce combat with a great clawed crab upon the mudflat. The students, moved by its boldness, carried it back to the Archives and gave it a place in the Dining Hall.
With Roe around, the nighttime pests that had plagued the Dining Hall found nowhere left to hide. The occasional student who crept in after dark in search of something to eat was likewise sent retreating in haste by Roe's bark.
Thanks to the generous feeding from masters and students in the Dining Hall, Roe grew ever more particular in its tastes. It would not eat from soiled vessels, nor take food from an open hand. Only when a proper bowl was filled and set before it would it lower its paws in what seemed a salute of thanks, and only then would it begin to eat.
Everyone said that Roe had learned propriety since joining the academy, and was a fine dog of the school. Roe understood none of it, and simply wagged its tail.
The days passed like food in a bowl, heaped full, then emptied to the bottom. Now Roe had grown old, and no longer made its rounds of the Dining Hall.
It lay often beneath the Flowering Tree, eyes half-closed.
Amid the riot of purple blossoms, it seemed as though it had become once more the bold little dog of those muddy days gone by, unafraid of the crab's claws, unafraid of the crashing waves.

一曰地势之枢。滹沱河横贯燕赵，直通幽冀，得南岸者，则可直驱河朔，逐鹿中原。
二曰兵形之险。滹沱河水量丰沛，夏日洪水漫天，冬日冰封千里。若能据守南岸，以待天时，则北境之敌，不攻自退。
三曰囤粮之脉。南岸土地丰腴，广种粮粟，粮道纵横，以资三军。盘踞南岸之军，可扼运粮之命脉。
今南北交恶，风云莫测。若能重锁滹沱南岸，以为屏障，则中原门户可固矣。
en:
The Hutuo rises in the north from Mount Taixi, runs south through Zhending Prefecture, and empties east into the Bohai Sea. Its waters never cease, its course long and far reaching. Throughout the ages, the south bank has always been ground for which armies contend. As for the reason, after surveying the matter again and again, I would put it down to three points:
First, it is the key to the terrain.
The Hutuo cuts across the lands of Yan and Zhao and opens straight into You and Ji. Whoever holds the south bank can drive directly into Heshuo and contend for the Central Plains.
Second, it is a position of natural military advantage.
The Hutuo runs deep and full. In summer, floodwaters spread far and wide. In winter, the river freezes for miles. If one can hold the south bank and wait on the season, then the enemy from the north may be made to fall back without a fight.
Third, it is the artery of grain supply.
The south bank is rich and fertile, planted widely with grain and millet. Supply routes crisscross the region, feeding the three armies. Any force that holds the south bank can choke the flow of grain.
Now north and south are at odds, and the times are uncertain. If the south bank of the Hutuo can once again be firmly secured as a barrier, then the gateway to the Central Plains may be held fast.

zh:
行商有时候和赌博没什么两样，计算概率，衡量投入和风险，然后赌上可以接受的本钱。概率不可能是百分百，所以经商总是有赚有赔。
康珍珠不喜欢赌博，她觉得商人就应该等待，观察，一旦得到了可靠的消息，就全力出手。只要消息新且真实，运作得当，生意就不会亏本。
窣利人，永远不会做亏本的买卖。
当年她倾尽商队积蓄建造珍珠舟，便是获得了波陈、於突等多方的路子，就差大唐驻军的庇佑了。听说那个军队穷得叮当响，只要交易能谈成，定能赚回百倍利润。 
可唐人竟然质疑窣利人的经商本事？
“您怎么不信我呢？”年轻的康珍珠在关隘堵住郭昕，“你们那点军饷顶个屁用！你把军饷银子投给我，还有你军队的印信，我把玉石倒腾去於突，回来十倍还您！”
“康商主，这世上没有永远赚的买卖。”
“郭将军，您带兵能天天打胜仗，凭啥不信我做生意能稳赚？”
“打仗也会输的……输了就用命守。”
“……”
康珍珠忍了又忍，反复告诉自己，眼前这人是丝路上的通行证，波陈要讨好，於突要打点，大唐那边更不能得罪...... 
她再次换上笑脸："将军放心，该交的税一个子也不少！这不就是想带您一起发财嘛......" 
"就算...就算真亏了，我砸锅卖铁也给您补上！" 
"税照交，钱不投，印不借。"郭昕的脸色没有丝毫的改变。 
康珍珠愁得仿佛看到了满头都是白色的兔子在乱飞————光靠交税维持的关系，在这混乱的地方里能撑几天？ 
当晚，康珍珠就拎着一壶三勒浆翻上了城头。月光把将军的影子拉得老长，酒碗碰得叮当响，一杯一杯酒下肚，一句一句朋友唤着，终于……康珍珠的生意还是没有谈成，反倒云里雾里地与他签了一份新契——她，居无定所的窣利商人，居然要出钱给唐人挖井！虽说井是给过路的同族用的，井水灌溉的绿洲会是窣利人的聚集地，可那汉人将军嘴里的月亮啊、故乡什么的，就像吃不到的馕饼，谁知道会不会亏本……
窣利人的赚钱本事，这回真要栽到沙子里了？康珍珠醉醺醺地靠着骆驼，朦胧间似乎真看到了月光里满地胡杨树的影子，忽然觉得......这次交易应该还是稳赚不赔。
en:
Sogdians never make losing deals. Back then, she spent the caravan's entire savings to build the Pearl Boat, having secured channels with the Bodchen, Utuk, and others. All she needed was the protection of the Tang garrison. She heard that army was dirt poor. If a deal could be struck, profits would multiply a hundredfold. 

Yet the Tang people actually doubted Sogdians' business acumen.

"How can you not believe me?" Kang Zhenzhu blocked Guo Xin at the pass. "Your meager pay is useless! Give me your silver and your army's seal, and I'll trade jade to the Utuk. Tenfold returns, I promise!"

"Kang, you can't win forever in this world."

"General Guo, you lead troops to victory every day. Why doubt I can turn a sure profit?"

"Battles can be lost too... When they are, we defend with our lives."

"..."

Kang Zhenzhu swallowed her anger, reminding herself: This man is her pass on the Silk Road. She needed to please the Bodchen, grease palms in Utuk, and never offend the Tang...

She forced a smile. "General, rest assured, not a coin of tax will go unpaid! I only want to make us both rich..."

"Even if we lose money, I'll sell everything to make it right!"

"Pay your taxes. But no investments, no seal."

Guo Xin's expression didn't flicker.

That night, Kang Zhenzhu hauled a jug of wine up the city wall. Moonlight stretched the general's shadow long. Cups clinked as they drank, round after round, calling each other "friend" with every toast... 

Yet still, the deal fell through.

Instead, half-drunk and hazy, she signed a new contract: she, a rootless Sogdian merchant, would fund well-digging for the Tang! The wells were for her fellow traders, sure, and the watered oasis would become a Sogdian hub. But that Han general's talk of moons and homelands felt like flatbread forever out of reach. Who knew if she'd profit or lose?

Was Sogdian business prowess truly to fail this time?

Drunk, Kang Zhenzhu leaned against her camel. Through the haze, she seemed to see poplar shadows dancing in the moonlight. And suddenly... she felt certain this deal would pay off after all.

宋代贵族阶级，鹰猎是一种常见的娱乐方式。特别是以北方为代表的草原民族，更是盛行一时。据史料记载，从辽开始直至清代，鹰中的神俊者’海东青‘便被选为贡品。民间甚至摸索出一套鹰猎的习俗：捕鹰，熬鹰，驯鹰，放鹰，可见鹰猎文化在当时比较成熟。
en:
This old man stirs his youthful fervor again, a yellow hound to the left, a falcon held high to the right. 

The nobles of Song dynasty were known to entertain themselves with falconry, and the nomad tribes on the northern steppes loved it even more. From Liao dynasty to Qing dynasty, gyrfalcons were considered the most fierce and requisitioned as imperial tributes. Falcon handlers developed a set of techniques: capturing, taming, manning and casting; further testifies the popularity of falconry at that time.

【闵公第四】

元年，春，王正月。
公何以不言即位？继弑君不言即位。孰继？继子般也。孰弑子般？庆父也。杀公子牙，今将尔，季子不免。庆父弑君，何以不诛？将而不免，遏恶也。既而不可及，因狱有所归，不探其情而诛焉，亲亲之道也。恶乎归狱？归狱仆人邓扈乐。曷为归狱仆人邓扈乐？庄公存之时，乐曾淫于宫中，子般执而鞭之。庄公死，庆父谓乐曰："般之辱尔，国人莫不知，盍弑之矣？"使弑子般，然后诛邓扈乐而归狱焉。季子至而不变也。
〇齐人救邢。
〇夏，六月，辛酉，葬我君庄公。
〇秋，八月，公及齐侯盟于洛姑。
〇季子来归。
其称季子何？贤也。其言来归何？喜之也。
〇冬，齐仲孙来。
齐仲孙者何？公子庆父也。公子庆父则曷为谓之齐仲孙？系之齐也。曷为系之齐？外之也。曷为外之？春秋为尊者讳，为亲者讳，为贤者讳。子女子曰："以春秋为春秋，齐无仲孙，其诸吾仲孙与？"
……
en:
【Duke Min, Volume Four】

First year, spring, the king's first month.
Why does the Duke not mention his accession? After a ruler has been assassinated, one does not mention accession. Whose succession does he continue? He continues the succession of Zi Ban. Who assassinated Zi Ban? Qing Fu. When he killed Prince Ya, intending to act but was prevented, Ji Zi was not spared. Qing Fu assassinated the ruler—why was he not executed? Because his intention was thwarted and he was not spared, this curbed evil. Afterwards, it could not be pursued, and since the crime had a designated culprit, they did not probe the truth but executed someone, following the principle of kinship. Where was the crime attributed? It was attributed to the servant Deng Hu Le. Why was the crime attributed to the servant Deng Hu Le? During Duke Zhuang's lifetime, Le had once committed adultery in the palace; Zi Ban seized and whipped him. When Duke Zhuang died, Qing Fu said to Le: "Ban humiliated you, and no one in the state is unaware—why not assassinate him?" He had Zi Ban killed, then executed Deng Hu Le and attributed the crime to him. When Ji Zi arrived, nothing was changed.
〇The people of Qi rescued Xing.
〇Summer, sixth month, Xinyou, we buried our ruler Duke Zhuang.
〇Autumn, eighth month, the Duke formed an alliance with the Marquis of Qi at Luogu.
〇Ji Zi came to return.
Why is he called Ji Zi? Because he was worthy. Why does it say "came to return"? Because it was a cause for joy.
〇Winter, Zhong Sun of Qi came.
Who is Zhong Sun of Qi? He is Prince Qing Fu. If he is Prince Qing Fu, why is he called Zhong Sun of Qi? Because he is tied to Qi. Why is he tied to Qi? To distance him. Why distance him? The Spring and Autumn Annals conceals for the honored, conceals for the kin, and conceals for the worthy. The Woman said: "Using the Spring and Autumn Annals as the Spring and Autumn Annals, Qi has no Zhong Sun—could he be our Zhong Sun?"
……

《青海波》是唐代青海地区少数民族吐谷浑的民间舞蹈，唐玄宗时期中原与西域的文化交流非常繁盛，因此出生西域碎叶城的李白也十分喜爱这种风格的音乐，他的诗篇《东山吟》就留有这一句“酣来自作青海舞，秋风吹落紫绮冠。” 另根据唐朝人魏万的《李翰林集序》记载:“饮数斗，醉则奴丹砂抚青海波。满堂不乐，白宰酒则乐”。
此曲存于《博雅笛谱》。
en: Dance of Azure Waves is a traditional folk dance of the Tuyuhun people, an ethnic minority from the Qinghai region during the Tang dynasty. During Emperor Xuanzong's reign, cultural exchange between the Central Plains and the Western Regions flourished immensely. Because of this, the great poet Li Bai, who was born in the western city of Suyab, cherished this musical style. In his poem Chant of the Eastern Mountain, he wrote: "In my drunken glee, I dance the Azure Waves; the autumn wind blows off my purple silken cap." Furthermore, according to Wei Wan's Preface to the Collection of Hanlin Scholar Li, "After drinking several measures of wine, in his intoxication, he would have his servant Dansha play the Azure Waves. When the entire hall fell out of spirits, Li Bai would pour the wine, and joy would return." The musical score is preserved in the Boya Flute Score.

其一，入茧。入茧三十日尸解，旧骸灭而新体成。
其二，旧茧。此条最为紧要——旧茧万不可弃。旧躯虽寂灭，然气血未绝。须每三日归茧一次，取精血服之，方可长驻不衰。
其三，庄中人事。我已载明庄中上下诸人身份、来历，见后页，如有需要翻看便可。

若你正读此书，说明术法已成。以上三条，重中之重是归茧取血，切记，切记。
en:
The Post-Ritual Directives: ...I have no way of knowing what will happen to my mind once I enter the cocoon. Just in case, I am writing down the most vital information here for my future self to read.
1. Incubation: It takes thirty days inside the cocoon to shed the mortal shell. The old body dissolves, and a new form is born.
2. The Old Cocoon: This is the most critical rule of all. Never throw the old cocoon away. The original body may be dead, but its lifeblood hasn't dried up. You must return to the cocoon every three days to extract and drink its blood. It is the only way to sustain your new, immortal form.
3. Villa Staff: I have documented the identities and backgrounds of everyone living on the estate on the following pages. Use it as a refresher if you need it.

If you are reading this, the ritual was a success. Of the three rules above, returning to the cocoon for the blood is by far the most important. Never, ever forget this.

en:
Dear Wanderer,
(My two brothers are both illiter-rats, so I am acting as the "ghost-scrub" for this letter.)
The new year is coming. We three brothers have each found new gigs. Lately, Zhang Hu has been trying to read; he shows signs of becoming a culcherd person like me. My heart is truly strained! Zhang Bao is also no longer acting "crumpled" and has become much more stable. I even tried cooking rice one grain at a time, but alas, the iron wok was not up to the task. Finally, the pot shattered!
As such, so now we've got all this New Year's food and supplies with nowhere to go. We have attached them for the wanderers, hoping they bring you the blessings of a festive reunion.
With great respect, Zhang Long, Zhang Hu, and Zhang Bao

不同性别对应外观转化：若外观道具具有不同性别的版本，则会在转换后直接适配当前性别；若外观道具只拥有单性别版本，则转换性别后外观会暂时失效。
服装染色数据处理：原性别外观染色数据保留。首次转换性别时，根据原外观每一套染色方案最近一次消耗的染色道具，补偿对应的限时染色道具。再次转换性别时，将会只会补偿两次转换性别之间每一套染色方案最近一次消耗的染色道具。消耗限时道具进行染色，则转换性别时不会进行补偿。
发型染色数据处理：原性别染发数据保留。首次转换性别时，根据原性别每一套染发方案最近一次消耗的染发道具，补偿对应的限时染发道具。再次转换性别时，将会只会补偿两次转换性别之间每一套染色方案最近一次消耗的染色道具。消耗限时道具进行染发，则转换性别时不会进行补偿。
裁造数据处理：原性别裁造数据保留，并且现有裁造直接转换为对应性别时装的裁造方案。少量时装仅存在单性别裁造方案，则转换性别时不进行补偿。
饰品方寸移形数据处理：原性别方寸移形数据保留；在首次转换性别完成后，现性别的方寸移形数据将会重置。
妆容数据处理：原性别妆容数据保留；在首次转换性别完成后，现性别的妆容数据将会重置。
捏脸数据处理：性别转换时可以重新捏脸，原性别的捏脸数据不会直接套用至新性别；原性别捏脸数据以及槽位上限保留。
en:
Appearance Conversion: If a cosmetic item has cross-type version, it will automatically adapt to your new body type. If the item can only be used in a single body type, it will temporarily become unavailable after changing.
Outfit Dye Data: Dye data from your original body type will be preserved. For your first body type swap, you will be compensated with corresponding limited-time dye items based on the most recent dye materials consumed for each dye preset. On subsequent body swaps, compensation will only be provided for the most recent dye materials consumed for each outfit preset between the two changes. If you use limited-time dye items, no compensation will be given.
Hairstyle Dye Data: Hair dye data from your original body type will be preserved. For your first body type swap, you will be compensated with corresponding limited-time hair dye items based on the most recent hair dye materials consumed for each hairstyle dye preset. On subsequent body type swaps, compensation will only be provided for the most recent dye materials consumed for each hairstyle dye preset between the two changes. If you used limited-time dye items, no compensation will be given.
Outfit Customization Data: Outfit customization data from your original body type will be preserved. Existing custom outfits will automatically adapt to your new body type. Some outfits only have customization option for a single body type; no compensation will be provided in such cases.
Accessory Position: Position data from your original body type will be preserved. After your body swap, your Position data will be renewed.
Makeup Data: Makeup settings from your original body type will be preserved. After your body swap, your Makeup data will be renewed.
Face Customization Data: You will be able to customize your appearance again when swapping body types. Face data from your original body type will not be directly applied to the new body type. However, your original face data and slot limits will be preserved.

zh:
唐·李白
君不见，黄河之水天上来，奔流到海不复回。
君不见，高堂明镜悲白发，朝如青丝暮成雪。
人生得意须尽欢，莫使金樽空对月。
天生我材必有用，千金散尽还复来。
烹羊宰牛且为乐，会须一饮三百杯。
岑夫子，丹丘生，将进酒，杯莫停。
与君歌一曲，请君为我倾耳听。
钟鼓馔玉不足贵，但愿长醉不复醒。
古来圣贤皆寂寞，惟有饮者留其名。
陈王昔时宴平乐，斗酒十千恣欢谑。
主人何为言少钱，径须沽取对君酌。
五花马，千金裘，呼儿将出换美酒，与尔同销万古愁。
en:
Li Bai (Tang Dynasty)
Do you not see the Yellow River come from the sky, rushing into the sea and never come back?
Do you not see the mirrors bright in chambers high, grieve over your snow-white hair though once it was silk-black?
When hopes are won, oh! Drink your fill in high delight, and never leave your wine-cup empty in moonlight!
Heaven has made us talents, we're not made in vain. a thousand gold coins spent, more will turn up again.
Kill a cow, cook a sheep and let us merry be, and drink three hundred cupfuls of wine in high glee!
Dear friends of mine, cheer up, cheer up! I invite you to wine. Do not put down your cup!
I will sing you a song, please hear, O hear! Lend me a willing ear!
What difference will rare and costly dishes make? I only want to get drunk and never to wake.
How many great men were forgotten through the ages? But great drinkers are more famous than sober sages.
The Prince of Poets feasted in his palace at will, drank wine at ten thousand a cask and laughed his fill.
A host should not complain of money he is short, to drink with you I will sell things of any sort.
My fur coat worth a thousand coins of gold, and my flower-dappled horse may be sold, to buy good wine that we may drown the woe age-old.

江南好，山没清波内，帆在浮云中。
舟楫交错，水肆临风，如此大好风光，怎可无美酒助兴？一抹青衣掠过乌篷船头，那本该领路之人，竟逃之夭夭。

此番江南初见，穿花影，掠溪光，尽惹酒香满袖。且以此杯折飞花——江南无所有，聊赠一枝春。

Boats cross the waterways, and a breeze stirs the waterfront taverns. A view like this calls for a drink. A flash of blue robes passes the bow of a canopied boat, and your supposed guide is gone.
You give chase through the winding waterways, racing across the waves until you finally catch up with the elusive wine lover.
And so your days in Jiangnan begin, with blossoms overhead, sunlight dancing on the streams, and the scent of wine lingering on your sleeves. Raise a cup as the flowers drift by. What better gift of spring could Jiangnan offer?

zh:
黄止水五十岁那年，青州涌泉镇的松烟阁挂起了白幡。
可这白幡下无哭声，反是唢呐高亢，鼓点如雨。一场丧事，吵闹如同喜宴。
黄止水在棺椁前，一身素麻，席地而坐，双手却热烈地敲着鼓盆。
堂前棺木空荡，外头由远及近传来锣鼓之声。

“喜事啊！傻徒弟，吹个乐呵的！”祝丑公摇摇晃晃，身后跟着个吹唢呐的男人。
这话是说给满堂宾客，更是说给黄止水。

五十载浮沉，如江河上漂流的木盆，晃晃荡荡，终是靠了岸。
早年，他凭巧手在右藏库雕玉刻金，仿古摹今，连传国玺的纹路都能复刻得分毫不差。
那时，世人赞他“鬼工”，他自己也信。
偏偏冯道那人说：“工巧易得，学问难求。”
黄止水当时只哂笑，笑这姓冯的迂腐。乱世之中，银钱才是真学问。

可这几十年的往来，是做不得假的。
是，他黄止水有时是烦冯道，烦他絮叨。
但冯道死前那封绝笔信，却让他立了很久。
信中无甚大事，只絮絮说着山水之趣，治学之乐。以及最后，落下的一个“真”字。
赝替真品，暗通关节，松烟阁明里济民，暗里敛财……这些年，他一步一步，得到很多，可却也更空。

罢了，罢了！
就用这场丧礼喜宴，为自己送行吧。也算为那长乐老送行了。

身后，白幡应着锣鼓声、笑歌猎猎作响，黄止水笑着往外，这是他几十载来，步子最轻快的一次。

棺中无尸。
世间再无黄止水。
en:
In the fiftieth year of Huang Zhishui's life, white mourning banners were hoisted at the Pinemist Pavilion in Wellspring Town of Qingzhou. Yet beneath these banners, there was no weeping; instead, the suona wailed in high pitches, and the drumbeats fell like driving rain. It was a funeral, yet as boisterous as a wedding feast.
Clad in coarse mourning hemp, Huang Zhishui sat on the ground before the coffin, his hands passionately beating the clay basin. The coffin in the hall stood empty. From outside, the clamor of gongs and drums approached from afar.
"This is a joyous occasion! You silly disciple, play something cheerful!" Zhu Chougong staggered in, followed closely by a man blowing the suona. These words were meant for the hall full of guests, but even more so for Huang Zhishui.
Fifty years of drifting in the martial world, like a wooden basin tossing upon the river, had finally found the shore.
In his early years, relying on his deft hands, he carved jade and engraved gold in the Imperial Treasury. He imitated the ancients and copied his contemporaries; he could even replicate the intricate veins of the Imperial Seal without a single flaw. In those days, the world praised his craftsmanship as the work of spirits, and he himself believed it.
Yet that man, Feng Dao, had said, "Cunning craftsmanship is easily acquired; true wisdom is hard to seek."
At the time, Huang Zhishui only sneered, laughing at the man for his pedantry. In a world of chaos, wealth was the only true wisdom.
But the decades of their association could not be faked. True, he, Huang Zhishui, was sometimes annoyed by Feng Dao, weary of his endless chattering. However, Feng Dao's final letter before his death made him stand in silence for a very long time. The letter contained no matters of great consequence, only rambling about the charm of mountains and rivers, and the joy of scholarly pursuit. And at the very end, it left behind a single word, "Truth."
Forging counterfeits to replace the genuine, secretly pulling strings and bribing officials; Pinemist Pavilion aided the commoners in the light, but amassed wealth in the dark... Over these years, step by step, he had gained much, yet he felt all the more empty.
Enough, let it be!
Let this joyous funeral serve as a send-off for himself. It could also be considered a final send-off for Elder Changle.
Behind him, the white banners fluttered fiercely in the wind, echoing the gongs, drums, and laughter. Huang Zhishui smiled and walked out. It was the lightest his steps had been in decades.
The coffin held no corpse. The world held Huang Zhishui no more.

数日不见，小八又有了新点子， 一个将音乐传播到晦谷之外的新发明。但他陷入了困难，这次要放什么旋律呢？晦谷的大家都没出过远门，小八只好向你请教：你去过那么多地方，有没有听到过哪首曲子，最最最好听，最最最忘不掉？
有，当然有：#Y【月儿弯弯照秦川……】听罢，小八抬头望天，点了点他的铜脑壳。#E
你将歌谣唱了出来，小八摇晃起了他的铜脑壳，沉醉其中。
“太太太太好听了！”待你唱完，小八不禁发出了感慨。
如此美妙的音乐，当然要用在改造后的八音盒上。
不久之后，小八邀请你来欣赏他的最新大作！
这回，他把八音盒嵌进了火箭中，又把火箭绑在了自己身上。
继“一飞冲天”后，小八的最最新发明——“飞唱不可”再次响彻山中。
——祝小八再次顺利降落！
en:
After just a few days apart, Xiaoba has already dreamed up another new mechanism, which is meant to send music beyond the borders of Mirkvale. But he has run into a problem: what tune should it play? No one in Mirkvale has ever traveled far, so he comes to you for help. "You've been to so many places," he says. "Have you ever heard a melody, one so beautiful, so unforgettable, that it lingers in your heart forever?"
Yes, of course: #Y[The crescent moon shines over Qinchuan...] When he hears it, Xiaoba looks up and nods his little bronze head.#E
You begin to sing, and Xiaoba's little bronze head starts swaying gently from side to side, utterly lost in the music.
"It's so, so, so, so beautiful!" he blurts out the moment you finish.
A melody like that belongs in nothing less than his newly upgraded music box.
Not long afterward, Xiaoba invites you to admire his latest masterpiece!
This time, he has fitted the music box into a flaming arrow and then strapped the arrow to himself.
After "Skyward Soar," Xiaoba's newest invention, "Flying Singer," once again rings through the mountains.
May Xiaoba make another safe landing!

zh:
杜辰非做了一辈子的刀客。只不过，前半辈子拿的是杀人的刀，后半辈子提的是切肉的刀。
前半辈子，他提着一柄钢刀，除了四海任侠、劫富济贫，唯一的爱好便是大口吃肉。近身肉搏没吃过亏的他，最后却倒在契丹骑兵的冷箭之下。
昏昏沉沉不知睡了多久，他忽而闻到一阵扑鼻的肉香，睁开眼睛，见一个老人提着肉条走过。老人见他醒来，便也拿了两片肉脯给他，又向他讲起事情的始末。
原来此地名唤镇戍仓，是滹沱一带的粮食大营，老人姓张，在这里已摆了二十多年的肉铺，大家都喊他老张头。近日契丹南侵，营里加强了警戒。老张头与营里弟兄一同在外巡逻时，碰到个昏死过去了的侠客，连忙将他拖了回去。
杜辰非一边听，一边往嘴里塞肉脯吃，这种做法他此前从未尝过，只觉得口感独特，精神大振。他一个鲤鱼打挺翻下床，言明包裹里还有从贪官家里抢来的银子，求老张头传授做法。
老人朝他挥了挥手，说他若有心想学，一个子儿都不要。不过这五味脯是独门秘方。要学，便要在这继承老头的肉铺。
杜辰非摸了摸腰间的刀，想着自己才被契丹狗贼暗算，这笔账非算清楚不可。老头似是看出他的犹豫，于是与他立下一个承诺——
小后生，若用这把刀，再杀一百个虏人，可愿回来继承老张头的摊子？
空气里的香味愈发浓郁，杜辰非把头点了又点。
成交。
en:
Du Chenfei had been a bladesman his entire life. Only, in the first half of his life, he wielded a blade to kill; in the latter half, he lifted a cleaver to cut meat.
In his early years, when he wielded a steel broadsword, his only passion, aside from roaming the jianghu and robbing the rich to aid the poor, was eating meat by the mouthful. Having never suffered a loss in close combat, he was ultimately felled by a cold arrow from Khitan cavalry.
After sleeping in a groggy daze for who knows how long, he suddenly caught a mouthwatering aroma of meat. Opening his eyes, he saw an old man walking by, carrying strips of meat. Seeing him awake, the old man handed him two slices of dried meat and explained everything.
It turned out this place was called Toilgrain Barn, the main provision camp in the Hutuo region. The old man, surnamed Zhang, had run a meat stall here for over twenty years, and everyone called him Old Man Zhang. With the Khitan invading southward recently, the camp had heightened its vigilance. While patrolling outside with the camp brethren, Old Man Zhang had stumbled upon the unconscious wanderer and hurriedly dragged him back.
As Du Chenfei listened, he stuffed the dried meat into his mouth. He had never tasted anything prepared this way before, finding its unique texture greatly revitalizing to his spirits. He leaped out of bed with a kip-up, declaring that he still had silver in his bundle robbed from corrupt officials, and begged Old Man Zhang to teach him the recipe.
The old man waved his hand at him, saying that if he truly wanted to learn, he wouldn't charge a single coin.
However, this Five Flavor Jerky was an exclusive secret recipe. To learn it, he must inherit the old man's meat stall right here.
Du Chenfei touched the blade at his waist, thinking of how he had just been ambushed by the Khitan invaders; this was a score that had to be settled. The old man seemed to see through his hesitation and thus made a pact with him.
"Young lad, if you use this blade to kill another hundred foreign invaders, would you be willing to come back and inherit my stall?"
The savory aroma in the air grew even richer, and Du Chenfei nodded his head again and again.
"Deal."

en:
At the General's Shrine, you have seen the lively arena where villagers cheered, and met the blind, bewildered elder. You remember sharing a knapsack with her here, yet you still owe her a pine nut candy...
Now, things have changed and people are gone; the wind sweeps the wilderness, the moonlight traces the doors, and the night at the shrine is hushed and solemn. The general bled to bring this peace, and now he's barred from ever tasting it. Entering the General's Shrine once more, you only wish...
#YLet the storm cease. Fierce fires once burned down your hometown, yet now pear blossoms are budding anew. You hope the storms will calm, and your home in Qinghe will see no more turmoil.#E
You bow solemnly, just as Uncle Jiang asked of you many years ago. You witnessed that story unfold across Qinghe, and unknowingly became a part of it yourself. The general fighting to the death in blood-stained armor; this is loyalty. The warrior casting aside his name and riding north in disguise; this is righteousness. zh:
立契人林澜、林舟，今与王天度立约。显德五年五月，三人共乘一舟，出洋寻宝。王天度为舟主，林澜、林舟为舵师。此番出海，为期一月，自起锚之日算起，不论得宝与否，一月之内必返。
先付铜钱叁贯，为林澜、林舟共得。日后寻得宝船，另赏银帛，数目另议。若月内未得宝船而返，王天度仍须给付余钱拾贰贯，不得拖欠。
恐后无凭，故立此契为证。
en:
We, Lin Lan and Lin Zhou, hereby enter into an agreement with Wang Tiandu. On this fifth month of the fifth year of Xiande, we three shall set sail in search of treasure. Wang Tiandu shall act as captain, with Lin Lan and Lin Zhou as helmsmen. This voyage shall last exactly one month from the day we weigh anchor. Treasure or not, we are bound to return within that time.
An upfront payment of three strings of copper coins has been made, to be shared by Lin Lan and Lin Zhou. Should the treasure ship be found, additional rewards of silver and silk will be negotiated. Should we return empty-handed within the month, Wang Tiandu remains obligated to pay the outstanding balance of twelve strings of copper coins in full.
Signed and sealed as proof, lest there be any dispute hereafter.

zh:
游侠敬启：
眼瞅着又到了年末，老朽先给游侠拜个早年啦！
福、禄、寿那三个娃娃神神秘秘的，非说要与你“共谋大业”，硬是缠着老朽动笔写信，更重要的是，把“见面情报”带上。
<IMAGE id='im1' image_url='https://h72.fp.ps.netease.com/file/697b4011d5ea5f258f5e2cafKDh0Q83h07' size='1920*1080' color='255;255;255')'></IMAGE>
墨迹未干，小家伙们又凑上来了，让老朽一字不差把消息带到：
你要问这幅画是什么意思？……我也没弄清呢！
这三个小家伙跟老朽卖关子，只塞给我一幅画，说是随信寄去，游侠一看便知，马上就会来找她们了。
刚写几句，小家伙们又凑上来了，让老朽一字不差地记下：
小福：大个子！新年要到啦，找我们，办大事！
小禄：这计划不能让旁人知道。接头时……记得要对暗号。
小寿：我来喊！口号——鼠鼠生威！
<IMAGE id='im2' image_url='https://h72.fp.ps.netease.com/file/697b40224f471ee5c44a504epE8Hi3zP07' size='1920*1080' color='255;255;255')'></IMAGE>
我正写着呢，孩子们又涂了一幅，说这幅更厉害，你看完肯定马不停蹄跑来见面……喏，就是这张了。
至于约见的时间地点……老朽一头雾水，不过，想必难不倒游侠！
于此搁笔，再祝新年安康，大吉大利！
en:
Dear Wanderer,
The year-end is upon us, and I wish to offer you my New Year greetings ahead of time!
Those three little ones, Fu, Lu, and Shou, are being quite mysterious, insisting on "planning something grand" with you. They've pestered me into writing this letter.
<IMAGE id='im1' image_url='https://h72.fp.ps.netease.com/file/697b4011d5ea5f258f5e2cafKDh0Q83h07' size='1920*1080' color='255;255;255')'></IMAGE>
The ink has barely dried, yet the little kids have crowded around again, making sure I record their message word for word:
You wish to know the meaning of this painting? ...Truth be told, even I have yet to discern it!
The three of them are playing riddles with me; they simply thrust a painting into my hands and claimed that one look from you would suffice...
Little Fu: Big guy! The New Year is almost here! Come find us for some big business!
Little Lu: This plan must remain a secret. When we rendezvous... remember to give the secret signal.
Little Shou: Let me shout it! Our slogan, Rodent Rampage!
<IMAGE id='im2' image_url='https://h72.fp.ps.netease.com/file/697b40224f471ee5c44a504epE8Hi3zP07' size='1920*1080' color='255;255;255')'></IMAGE>
While I was writing, the children scribbled another one, claiming it is even more impressive and that you will surely come racing to meet them once you see it.
As for the time and place of your meeting... I am utterly bewildered, though I trust such a mystery will not be a trouble to you!
Happy New Year!

zh:
翻检古今志异之书，发觉一桩有趣之事：凡言深山遇仙者，十之七八竟落在浙中，颇可玩味。

譬如那“阮刘遇仙”：汉时刘晨、阮肇入天台山采药，迷路十三日，后遇二仙女邀入洞中，留住半年。出山一看，人间已过去十世。区区半载，换了百年光阴，乃仙家手段。

又有那“观棋烂柯”的故事：晋时王质入山砍柴，见二童子对弈。他在旁看了一局棋，低头一瞧，斧头的木柄已经烂了。回家去，世上竟无一人认得他。一局棋的工夫，人间已是沧海桑田。

两桩事，一在台州天台，一在衢州石室，皆是浙中深山。看来这浙地山中，自古便多有仙缘。

哈，如今又要多一桩了。
en:
Reading through old tomes and folktales, I noticed a fascinating pattern: nearly every legend of a mortal meeting an immortal in the deep mountains takes place right here in central Zhejiang. Quite a coincidence.
Take the tale of Liu and Ruan. During the Han Dynasty, Liu Chen and Ruan Zhao wandered into Tiantai Mountain to pick herbs and lost their way for thirteen days. Two immortal maidens found them and invited them into their cave for half a year. When the men finally returned home, ten generations had passed. Six months traded for centuries, such is the power of the divine.
Then there is the Legend of the Rotted Axe. In the Jin Dynasty, a woodcutter went into the mountains and found two youths playing chess. He stopped to watch a single match. When he looked down, his axe handle had rotted to dust. He returned home to find not a single living soul recognized him. In the span of one game, the mortal world had completely moved on.
One happened in Tiantai, Taizhou, and the other, in Shishi, Quzhou, both deep in the mountains of central Zhejiang. It seems this region has always drawn the divine.
Hah. Soon, there will be one more.

zh:
【雅·大雅】

文王之什

文王

文王在上，於昭于天。周虽旧邦，其命维新。有周不显，帝命不时。文王陟降，在帝左右。
亹亹文王，令闻不已。陈锡哉周，侯文王孙子。文王孙子，本支百世，凡周之士，不显亦世。
世之不显，厥犹翼翼。思皇多士，生此王国。王国克生，维周之桢；济济多士，文王以宁。
穆穆文王，于缉熙敬止。假哉天命，有商孙子。商之孙子，其丽不亿。上帝既命，侯于周服。
侯服于周，天命靡常。殷士肤敏，祼将于京。厥作祼将，常服黼冔。王之荩臣，无念尔祖。
无念尔祖，聿脩厥德。永言配命，自求多福。殷之未丧师，克配上帝。宜鉴于殷，骏命不易！
命之不易，无遏尔躬。宣昭义问，有虞殷自天。上天之载，无声无臭。仪刑文王，万邦作孚。

大明

明明在下，赫赫在上。天难忱斯，不易维王。天位殷适，使不挟四方。
挚仲氏任，自彼殷商，来嫁于周，曰嫔于京。乃及王季，维德之行。
大任有身，生此文王。维此文王，小心翼翼。昭事上帝，聿怀多福。厥德不回，以受方国。
天监在下，有命既集。文王初载，天作之合。在洽之阳，在渭之涘。
文王嘉止，大邦有子。大邦有子，伣天之妹。文定厥祥，亲迎于渭。造舟为梁，不显其光。
有命自天，命此文王。于周于京，缵女维莘。长子维行，笃生武王。保右命尔，燮伐大商。
殷商之旅，其会如林。矢于牧野，维予侯兴。上帝临女，无贰尔心。
牧野洋洋，檀车煌煌，驷騵彭彭。维师尚父，时维鹰扬。凉彼武王，肆伐大商，会朝清明。
……

生民之什

生民

厥初生民，时维姜嫄。生民如何？克禋克祀，以弗无子。履帝武敏歆，攸介攸止，载震载夙。载生载育，时维后稷。
诞弥厥月，先生如达。不坼不副，无菑无害，以赫厥灵。上帝不宁，不康禋祀，居然生子。
诞寘之隘巷，牛羊腓字之。诞寘之平林，会伐平林。诞寘之寒冰，鸟覆翼之。鸟乃去矣，后稷呱矣。实覃实訏，厥声载路。
诞实匍匐，克岐克嶷，以就口食。蓺之荏菽，荏菽旆旆。禾役穟穟，麻麦幪幪，瓜瓞唪唪。
诞后稷之穑，有相之道。茀厥丰草，种之黄茂。实方实苞，实种实褎。实发实秀，实坚实好。实颖实栗，即有邰家室。
诞降嘉种，维秬维秠，维穈维芑。恒之秬秠，是获是亩。恒之穈芑，是任是负，以归肇祀。
诞我祀如何？或舂或揄，或簸或蹂。释之叟叟，烝之浮浮。载谋载惟，取萧祭脂。取羝以軷，载燔载烈，以兴嗣岁。
卬盛于豆，于豆于登，其香始升。上帝居歆，胡臭亶时。后稷肇祀，庶无罪悔，以迄于今。

行苇

敦彼行苇，牛羊勿践履。方苞方体，维叶泥泥。戚戚兄弟，莫远具尔。或肆之筵，或授之几。
肆筵设席，授几有缉御。或献或酢，洗爵奠斝。醓醢以荐，或燔或炙。嘉肴脾臄，或歌或咢。
敦弓既坚，四鍭既钧，舍矢既均，序宾以贤。敦弓既句，既挟四鍭。四鍭如树，序宾以不侮。
曾孙维主，酒醴维醹，酌以大斗，以祈黄耇。黄耇台背，以引以翼。寿考维祺，以介景福。
……

荡之什

荡
荡荡上帝，下民之辟。疾威上帝，其命多辟。天生烝民，其命匪谌。靡不有初，鲜克有终。
文王曰咨，咨女殷商。曾是彊御？曾是掊克？曾是在位？曾是在服？天降滔德，女兴是力。
文王曰咨，咨女殷商。而秉义类，彊御多怼。流言以对。寇攘式内。侯作侯祝，靡届靡究。
文王曰咨，咨女殷商。女炰烋于中国。敛怨以为德。不明尔德，时无背无侧。尔德不明，以无陪无卿。
文王曰咨，咨女殷商。天不湎尔以酒，不义从式。既愆尔止。靡明靡晦。式号式呼。俾昼作夜。
文王曰咨，咨女殷商。如蜩如螗，如沸如羹。小大近丧，人尚乎由行。内奰于中国，覃及鬼方。
文王曰咨，咨女殷商。匪上帝不时，殷不用旧。虽无老成人，尚有典刑。曾是莫听，大命以倾。
文王曰咨，咨女殷商。人亦有言：颠沛之揭，枝叶未有害，本实先拨。殷鉴不远，在夏后之世。
抑
抑抑威仪，维德之隅。人亦有言：靡哲不愚，庶人之愚，亦职维疾。哲人之愚，亦维斯戾。
无竞维人，四方其训之。有觉德行，四国顺之。訏谟定命，远犹辰告。敬慎威仪，维民之则。
其在于今，兴迷乱于政。颠覆厥德，荒湛于酒。女虽湛乐从，弗念厥绍。罔敷求先王，克共明刑。
肆皇天弗尚，如彼泉流，无沦胥以亡。夙兴夜寐，洒扫庭内，维民之章。修尔车马，弓矢戎兵，用戒戎作，用逷蛮方。
质尔人民，谨尔侯度，用戒不虞。慎尔出话，敬尔威仪，无不柔嘉。白圭之玷，尚可磨也；斯言之玷，不可为也！
无易由言，无曰苟矣，莫扪朕舌，言不可逝矣。无言不雠，无德不报。惠于朋友，庶民小子。子孙绳绳，万民靡不承。
视尔友君子，辑柔尔颜，不遐有愆。相在尔室，尚不愧于屋漏。无曰不显，莫予云觏。神之格思，不可度思，矧可射思！
辟尔为德，俾臧俾嘉。淑慎尔止，不愆于仪。不僭不贼，鲜不为则。投我以桃，报之以李。彼童而角，实虹小子。
荏染柔木，言缗之丝。温温恭人，维德之基。其维哲人，告之话言，顺德之行。其维愚人，覆谓我僭。民各有心。
於乎小子，未知臧否。匪手携之，言示之事。匪面命之，言提其耳。借曰未知，亦既抱子。民之靡盈，谁夙知而莫成？
昊天孔昭，我生靡乐。视尔梦梦，我心惨惨。诲尔谆谆，听我藐藐。匪用为教，覆用为虐。借曰未知，亦聿既耄。
於乎小子，告尔旧止。听用我谋，庶无大悔。天方艰难，曰丧厥国。取譬不远，昊天不忒。回遹其德，俾民大棘。
……

en:
【Ya · Daya】 Odes of King Wen King Wen King Wen is on high;
Oh! bright is he in heaven.
Though Zhou was an old state,
The [favouring] appointment lighted on it recently.
Illustrious was the House of Zhou,
And the appointment of God came at the proper season.
King Wen ascends and descends
On the left and the right of God. Full of earnest activity was King Wen,
And his fame is without end.
The gifts [of God] to Zhou
Extend to the descendants of King Wen; –
To the descendants of King Wen,
In the direct line and the collateral branches for a hundred generations.
All the officers of Zhou
Shall [also] be illustrious from age to age. They shall be illustrious from age to age,
Zealously and reverently pursuing their plans.
Admirable are the many officers,
Born in this royal kingdom.
The royal kingdom is able to produce them, –
The supporters of [the House of] Zhou.
Numerous is the array of officers,
And by them King Wen enjoys his repose. Profound was King Wen;
Oh! continuous and bright was his feeling of reverence.
Great is the appointment of Heaven!
There were the descendants of [the sovereigns] of Shang; –
The descendants of the sovereigns of Shang,
Were in number more than hundreds of thousands.
But when God gave the command,
They became subject to Zhou. They became subject to Zhou;
The appointment of Heaven is not constant.
The officers of Yin, admirable and alert,
Assist at the libations in our capital; –
They assist at those libations,
Always wearing the hatchets on their lower garment and their peculiar cap.
O ye loyal ministers of the king,
Ever think of your ancestor! Ever think of your ancestor,
Cultivating your virtue,
Always striving to accord with the will [of Heaven].
So shall you be seeking for much happiness.
Before Yin lost the multitudes,
[Its kings] were the assessors of God.
Look to Yin as a beacon; –
The great appointment is not easily [preserved]. The appointment is not easily [preserved];
Do not cause your own extinction.
Display and make bright your righteousness and name,
And look at [the fate of] Yin in the light of Heaven.
The doings of high Heaven
Have neither sound nor smell.
Take your pattern from King Wen,
And the myriad regions will repose confidence in you. Da Ming Illustrious was the [future] mother of Zhou,
Ren, the lady of Ji.
She came from Yin Shang,
And came to be married in Zhou.
She became the bride in the capital,
Along with Ji, the king.
The virtuous [lady] pursued her way. Great Ren became pregnant,
And gave birth to this King Wen.
This King Wen,
Watchfully and reverently,
With entire intelligence served God,
And so secured the great blessing.
His virtue was without deflection;
And in consequence he received [the allegiance of] the states from all quarters. Heaven surveyed this lower world;
And its appointment lighted [on King Wen].
In his early years,
It made for him a mate;
On the north of the Xiao,
On the banks of the Wei. King Wen made good his virtue;
The great state had a daughter.
The great state had a daughter,
Looking as if sent from Heaven.
The ceremonies of betrothal were determined,
And King Wen in person met her on the Wei.
Over it he made a bridge of boats;
The glory [of the occasion] was illustrious. The favouring appointment was from Heaven,
Giving the throne to our King Wen,
In the capital of Zhou.
The lady-successor was from Xin,
Its eldest daughter, who came to marry him.
She was blessed to give birth to King Wu,
Who was preserved, and helped, and received also the appointment,
And in accordance with it smote the great Shang. The troops of Yin Shang
Were collected like a forest,
And marshalled in the wilderness of Mu.
We rose [to the crisis]; – 'God is with you, '[said Shang-fu to the king],
'Have no doubts in your heart.' The wilderness of Mu spread out extensive;
Bright shone the chariots of sandal;
The teams of bays, black-maned and white-bellied, galloped along;
The Grand-Master Shang-fu
Was like an eagle on the wing,
Assisting King Wu,
Who at one onset smote the great Shang.
That morning's encounter was followed by a clear bright [day]. …… Odes of Sheng Min Sheng Min Who gave birth to our people?
It was Jiang Yuan.
How did she give birth to our people?
She had presented a pure offering and sacrificed,
That her childlessness might be taken away.
She then trod on a toe-print made by God, and was moved,
In the large place where she rested.
She became pregnant; she dwelt retired;
She gave birth to, and nourished [a son],
Who was Hou Ji. When she had fulfilled her months,
Her first-born son [came forth] like a lamb.
There was no bursting, nor rending,
No injury, no hurt; –
Showing how wonderful he would be.
Did not God give her the comfort?
Had He not accepted her pure offering and sacrifice,
So that thus easily she brought forth her son? He was placed in a narrow lane,
But the sheep and oxen protected him with loving care.
He was placed in a wide forest,
Where he was met with by the wood-cutters.
He was placed on the cold ice,
And a bird screened and supported him with its wings.
When the bird went away,
Hou Ji began to wail.
His cry was long and loud,
So that his voice filled the whole way. When he was able to crawl,
He looked majestic and intelligent.
When he was able to feed himself,
He fell to planting large beans.
The beans grew luxuriantly;
His rows of paddy shot up beautifully;
His hemp and wheat grew strong and close;
His gourds yielded abundantly. The husbandry of Hou Ji
Proceeded on the plan of helping [the growth].
Having cleared away the thick grass,
He sowed the ground with the yellow cereals.
He managed the living grain, till it was ready to burst;
Then he used it as seed, and it sprang up;
It grew and came into ear;
It became strong and good;
It hung down, every grain complete; –
And thus he was appointed lord of Tai. He gave his people the beautiful grains; –
The black millet, and the double-kernelled;
The tall red, and the white.
They planted extensively the black and the double-kernelled,
Which were reaped and stacked on the ground.
They planted extensively the tall red and the white,
Which were carried on their shoulders and backs,
Home for the sacrifices which he founded. And how as to our sacrifices [to him]?
Some hull [the grain]; some take it from the mortar;
Some sift it; some tread it.
It is rattling in the dishes;
It is distilled, and the steam floats about.
We consult; we observe the rites of purification;
We take southernwood and offer it with the fat;
We sacrifice a ram to the Spirit of the path;
We offer roast flesh and broiled; –
And thus introduce the coming year. We load the stands with the offerings,
The stands both of wood and of earthenware.
As soon as the fragrance ascends,
God, well pleased, smells the sweet savour.
Fragrant is it, and in its due season!
Hou Ji founded the sacrifice,
And no one, we presume, has given occasion for blame or regret in regard to it,
Down to the present day. Xing Wei Thick grow the rushes by the way;
The oxen and sheep should not trample them.
They are just bursting from the sheath,
And their leaves are soft and glossy.
Affectionate brothers,
Should not be distant towards one another.
Some spread the mats for them;
Some present them with the stools. The mats are spread, and the stools are set;
Attendants take their places.
The guests pledge one another;
The cups are washed and set down.
Pickled meat and minced meat are presented;
Roast meat and broiled.
There are dishes of spleen and tripe;
And there is singing and beating of drums. The bow of mulberry wood is strong,
And its four arrows are balanced.
The arrows are discharged, and all hit,
And the guests are arranged according to their skill.
The bow of mulberry wood is bent,
And the four arrows are shot.
The four arrows stand in the target,
And the guests are arranged so that none is slighted. Zeng Sun is the host;
The liquor is both sweet and good.
The large cup is filled,
And they pray for the hoary age.
The hoary age, with its bent back,
Is led on and supported.
Long life and old age are auspicious;
May they be grandly blessed! …… Odes of Dang Dang How great is God,
The ruler of men below!
How arrayed in terrors is God,
With many things irregular in his ordinations!
Heaven gave birth to the multitudes of the people,
But the nature it confers is not to be depended on.
All are good at first,
But few prove themselves to be so at the last. King Wen said, 'Alas!
Alas! you [sovereign of] Yin-Shang.
Strong and fierce are you,
And a man of violent hand.
You are in the highest place,
And hold the appointment [of Heaven],
But you have fallen into all these errors.
Heaven sent down this condition of disorder,
But you have increased it by your violence. King Wen said, 'Alas!
Alas! you [sovereign of] Yin-Shang.
You have held the righteous to be unrighteous,
And the violent you have deemed strong.
You have had slanderous flatterers,
And strong men of violence.
They have uttered their calumnies,
And you have not examined into them,
So that bandits and robbers
Have been raised to office.
They have violently abused and cursed [the people],
And there is no limit to their iniquity.' King Wen said, 'Alas!
Alas! you [sovereign of] Yin-Shang.
You have roared and blustered like a tiger,
Through the Middle Kingdom.
You have taken no account of the murmurs of the people,
And have held the discontented to be doing you good service.
You have not been enlightened in your virtue,
And so have had none near you who were not cringing and obsequious;
And you have had none to stand by you,
Who were not flatterers. King Wen said, 'Alas!
Alas! you [sovereign of] Yin-Shang.
Heaven did not let you go on drinking,
And yet you follow your wild courses.
You have gone astray in your conduct,
And have been disorderly morning and night.
You shout and roar,
Making the day into night. King Wen said, 'Alas!
Alas! you [sovereign of] Yin-Shang.
You are like the cicada,
Like the grasshopper,
Like boiling water,
Like bubbling soup.
Great and small are near to ruin,
And yet you still go on in your evil ways.
The rage [of the people] is extending through the Middle Kingdom,
And has reached the wild tribes. King Wen said, 'Alas!
Alas! you [sovereign of] Yin-Shang.
It is not that God is not [good] to you,
But you of Yin do not follow the old ways.
Though there are no old experienced men,
There are still the ancient statutes and laws.
But you will not listen to them,
And so your great appointment is being overthrown. King Wen said, 'Alas!
Alas! you [sovereign of] Yin-Shang.
People have a saying,
"When a tree falls utterly,
While its branches and leaves are yet uninjured,
It must first have been uprooted."
The beacon of Yin is not far distant; –
It is in the age of the [last] sovereign of Xia.' Yi Dignified and grave should be the demeanour,
As becomes the corner [of virtue].
People have a saying, –
'There is no wise man who is not [sometimes] stupid.'
The stupidity of the common man
Is from his natural defects.
The stupidity of the wise man
Is from his perverse adherence to his own views. There is nothing more powerful than the cultivation [of virtue],
To which all the people will become subject.
When there is the power of virtuous conduct,
All the states will become obedient.
With far-reaching plans and settled counsels,
He announces his instructions from time to time.
Reverently attending to his deportment,
He becomes a pattern to the people. But now in the present [king],
There is great disorder in the government,
And his virtue is all subverted.
He is sunk in wine,
And thinks only of pleasure and idleness.
He does not think of the inheritance of his ancestors,
Nor does he diffuse and make known their statutes.
He has not in himself any wise plans,
And so he has not the guidance of the law. Then let the great Heaven not regard him,
But like as when an overflowing stream
Sweeps all away, so let him perish.
Rise early and go to bed late,
Sprinkle and sweep your courtyard,
To be a pattern to the people.
Have in good order your chariots and horses,
Your bows and arrows, and weapons of war;
That you may be prepared for war,
And may keep at a distance the wild tribes of the south. Secure the peace of your people,
Be careful of your conduct,
And be prepared for unexpected events.
Be careful of what you say,
Be respectful in your demeanour,
In everything be gentle and good.
A flaw in a mace of white jade
May be ground away;
But for a flaw in speech
Nothing can be done. Do not say, 'This is of no importance.'
No one holds my tongue.
Words cannot be retracted.
There is no word but has its answer;
There is no action but has its recompense.
Be kind to friends and relatives,
And to the multitudes of the people.
Your descendants will continue your line,
And the myriad people will all be ruled by you. Look at your friends and associates,
And compose your countenance to gentleness.
There will be no error.
Look within your chamber;
Be free from shame even in its most secret corners.
Do not say, 'This place is not public.'
No one can see me.
The approaches of spiritual beings
Cannot be calculated;
How much less can they be slighted! Make your virtue illustrious,
Making it perfect and admirable.
Be careful of your outward behaviour,
And allow nothing wrong in your demeanour.
Do nothing wrong, and do no harm,
And few will not take you as their pattern.
When some one throws me a peach,
I require him with a plum.
That hornless calf
Would be used to gore the people. That soft and pliant wood
May be bound round with strings.
That mild and gentle man
Is the foundation of virtue.
If he be a wise man,
Tell him the ancient lessons,
And he will follow the course of virtue.
If he be a stupid man,
He will say that I am deceiving him.
The minds of the people are not the same. Alas! you child,
You do not know what is good and what is not good.
Not only do I lead you by the hand,
But I show you the affairs [of the government].
Not only do I face you and give you my instructions,
But I hold you by the ear.
If you say that you are not yet able [to attend to them],
You have already carried a child in your arms.
If the people are not self-possessed,
Who, beginning early, will become perfect? How bright is the great Heaven!
And I have no pleasure [in life].
I see you so dreamy and stupid,
And my heart is full of pain.
I instruct you with all earnestness;
But you listen to me with contempt.
You do not use my lessons as a rule;
But on the contrary you make a jest of them.
If you say that you are not yet able [to attend to them],
You are already old. Alas! you child,
I tell you the old rules.
If you will listen to my plans,
I hope you will have no great repentance.
Heaven is now sending down calamities,
And is about to destroy our state.
I take an example not far off; –
The great Heaven is not changeable.
If you pervert your virtue,
You will bring great distress on the people. …… Song

未署名的旧纸条

记住，照此而行：
一、阴市诸摊，只可看，不可取。
二、欲得烛火，须先齐五供。
三、五供为：白口、青丝、黑路、黄昏、红喜。

五、阴市有红喜。
