遥望洞庭山水翠，白银盘里一青螺。

钱塘湖春行
白居易
孤山寺北贾亭西，水面初平云脚低。
几处早莺争暖树，谁家新燕啄春泥。
乱花渐欲迷人眼，浅草才能没马蹄。
最爱湖东行不足，绿杨阴里白沙堤。

湖亭望水
白居易
久雨南湖涨，新晴北客过。
日沉红有影，风定绿无波。
岸没闾阎少，滩平船舫多。
可怜心赏处，其奈独游何。

【溪】

青溪
王维
言入黄花川，每逐青溪水。
随山将万转，趣途无百里。
声喧乱石中，色静深松里。
漾漾泛菱荇，澄澄映葭苇。
我心素已闲，清川澹如此。
请留盘石上，垂钓将已矣。

兴唐寺
李白
天台国清寺，天下称四绝。
我来举唐游，于中更无别。
蘖木划断云，高峰顶积雪。
槛外一条溪，几回流碎月。

溪涨
杜甫
当时浣花桥，溪水才尺馀。
白石明可把，水中有行车。
秋夏忽泛溢，岂惟入吾庐。
蛟龙亦狼狈，况是鳖与鱼。
兹晨已半落，归路跬步疏。
马嘶未敢动，前有深填淤。
青青屋东麻，散乱床上书。
不意远山雨，夜来复何如。
我游都市间，晚憩必村墟。
乃知久行客，终日思其居。

题元八溪居
白居易
溪岚漠漠树重重，水槛山窗次第逢。
晚叶尚开红踯躅，秋芳初结白芙蓉。
声来枕上千年鹤，影落杯中五老峰。
更愧殷勤留客意，鱼鲜饭细酒香浓。
en:
【Geography · Part Two】

【Lake】

Qi Lake
Wang Wei
Playing the flute, I reach the distant shore; at dusk, I bid farewell to my lord.
Looking back over the lake, green mountains roll with white clouds.

Accompanying the Governor of Jinan, My Granduncle, Boating on Magpie Mountain Lake
Li Bai
The lake stretches for thousands of miles, its shimmering light sways the emerald hills.
The moon rises just west of the lake, as I alone see Li Ying off on his return.

Viewing Dongting Lake
Liu Yuxi
Lake light and autumn moon blend in harmony, the calm surface like an unpolished mirror.
Gazing at Dongting's green hills and waters—a blue snail on a silver plate.

Spring Outing by Qiantang Lake
Bai Juyi
North of Gushan Temple, west of Jiating, the water's surface levels as cloud banks hang low.
In several spots, early orioles vie for warm branches; from whose house do new swallows peck spring mud?
Wild blooms begin to dazzle the eye, short grass just hides the horse's hooves.
Most fond of strolling east of the lake, not tiring of the white sand dike in the shade of green willows.

Viewing Water from a Lakeside Pavilion
Bai Juyi
Long rains have swollen the South Lake; a northern traveler passes by on a fresh clear day.
The sun sinks, red leaving a shadow; the wind calms, green without a ripple.
The shore submerged, few houses remain; the flats level, many boats and barges.
Alas, for the place that delights my heart, what can I do but wander alone?

【Stream】

Green Stream
Wang Wei
Entering the land of Yellow Flowers, I often follow the Green Stream's flow.
Winding with the hills for countless turns, the journey's delight lies not in the distance.
Sound clamors among chaotic rocks; colors rest serene in deep pines.
Rippling, it floats water chestnuts and duckweed; clear and bright, it mirrors reeds and rushes.
My heart has always been at ease, as tranquil as this clear stream.
Let me stay upon this flat rock, angling here until the end.

Xingtang Temple
Li Bai
Guoqing Temple on Tiantai Mountain is hailed as one of the Four Wonders under heaven.
I come to visit during the Tang, finding nothing else to compare.
Twisted trees cleave the parting clouds; snow caps the highest peak.
Beyond the railing, a single stream, its moonlight shattered by the current time and again.

Stream Rising
Du Fu
Back then at Huanhua Bridge, the stream was barely over a foot deep.
White stones gleamed, graspable; carts passed through the water.
Suddenly it overflowed in autumn and summer, flooding not just my hut.
Even the flood dragon was in distress, let alone turtles and fish.
By morning it had half receded, the path home sparse with careful steps.
My horse whinnies, not daring to move, for ahead lies deep silt.
Green hemp east of the house, books scattered on the bed.
Who would have thought of distant mountain rain? What will the night bring?
I wander the city's markets, resting at dusk in village outskirts.
Thus I know the long-time traveler thinks of home all day long.

Inscribed at Yuan the Eighth's Riverside Dwelling
Bai Juyi
Stream mist stretches vast, trees stand thick; waterside railings and mountain windows greet me in turn.
Late leaves still bloom with red azaleas; autumn blossoms first form white lotuses.
The cry of a thousand-year crane comes to my pillow; the shadow of Five Elders Peak falls into my cup.
I feel all the more ashamed of your earnest hospitality—fresh fish, fine rice, and fragrant, rich wine.
You two certainly do things your own way.

Young Master,
Today, while practicing the Five Animal Frolics, I somehow got it into my head that I was a toad. Good thing a few miracle doctors from Silver Needle were there to pull me out of it, or I might have lost this tiger's spirit of mine and changed my name into Zhang Toad. And if Tiger Fort turned into Toad Fort, what face would we have left in the jianghu?
Those doctors said it was a rare case. Thinking I was a toad, yet still roaring like a tiger loud enough to shake the hills. Said it wasn't even written in the medical texts, and that alone could count as their fee. But I can't let it go at that. I'd like to invite them to Blissful Retreat and treat them properly.
Could you advance me a month's wages? I'll pay it back in full when next month's pay comes in.

en:
Swallow,

I hope this letter finds you well. Your birthday comes round again before long.
Year after year, official duties keep me tied down, and even in the midst of endless work, there is only more work still.
I cannot come in person this time, though I imagine...
you must be quite used to that by now!
And yet, though I cannot be there myself, my heart is always with you.
May these words stand in place of my presence. From afar, I wish you health in the coming year and a smile that never leaves you.
Next time, we shall speak again. I promise.

(Note: This fledgling pigeon is only just learning the ways of the clouds, and may lose its path. I ask anyone who finds this letter to pass it on to Master Swallow. Next time, I shall surely repay the kindness. I promise.)

zh:
清河以北，有一渡，名千年渡。此地舟楫相连，传五代避乱之民，为求一隅之地而安家于此。渡中川流纵横，屡受洪灾之患。其民虽苦，鲜有离群索居者。
细而察之，盖因渡中行淫祀之故。其民曰，室虽陋，奉神女之例不减。身虽苦，崇神女之祀不灭。
问之何故，笑言人间虽苦，然天地横祸，万般种种，皆为神女之试。今桃源高悬于天，仙乡永离于地。只待历劫不灭，俟风起之日，可身随流云，达桃源仙乡，睥睨天地可矣。
余闻之哑然，世间之事，光怪陆离，何其荒诞。
乱世纷扰，人心惶然，民委身虚妄，乃民之错耶？
en:
North of Qinghe is a crossing called the Millennium Crossing. Legend says it was settled by refugees fleeing war during the Five Dynasties. Though floods often ravage the tangled waterways, most people stay.
The reason? They worship a goddess devoutly. Despite broken homes and hard lives, they never skip the rituals or incense as they believe disasters are tests from the goddess. They say Haven now hangs high in the heavens, an immortal realm severed from this earth. They need only endure these tribulations until the winds rise...
I couldn't help but smile at how strange these beliefs are.
In these turbulent times, hearts are filled with dread. If the people cast themselves into delusions, is the fault truly theirs?

en:
Etched with the words "Autumn Water," its gleam sharp and untouchable. 
This treasured sword, which Lan Ao paid a fortune for and later shattered in defiance, was once wielded by famed masters. 

The warrior wearied by service to a corrupt lord had lost touch with his own formidable palm technique. 
Bestowed the Autumn Water sword along with political favor, he abandoned his palms for steel. 
The sword was what preserved his dignity, the last thing that allowed him to call himself a "hero." 
But in the end, he surrendered even that—offering it up to someone else, hoping to escape the downfall of a disgraced minister, hoping simply to "remain in Chang'an." 
It was no different from the past few decades, when he had "offered" his skills to the powerful. 
Dress it up however one likes, the truth remains: it was servitude, quiet and humbled.

近日在聆杏村倒遇见一桩巧事——石某此番途径聆杏村，竟偶遇一同名同姓之人，此人亦是天泉弟子，亦结识一位操持家业的游侠，探问下才知，那位游侠名唤$C$L#Y$PN#E$C，同游侠你竟也十分相似，亦是一名心系苍生、不惧险阻的我辈同道。

天下虽大，这般巧合却也难得，想来也唯有”缘分“二字才可解释。

相谈之际，吾见那位石惊天似有挂心之事，原来是其友为探秘寻宝，平日时常攀岩涉险，衣衫多有刮蹭，归家时难免一身破缕，形容狼狈。他本想亲自去开封羽衣楼讨教缝补手艺，却总被杂务耽搁。

既是同门，这点小事何须纠结？索性替其跑一趟羽衣楼，向绣娘讨教些许缝补之法。若有所得，他日说不定也可为游侠分忧一二。

此事需费些时日，归期若晚，望君勿要为我担忧。

en:
To the Wanderer:
Is everything going smoothly with the Homestead? We haven't exchanged news in a long time, and you are constantly in my thoughts.
Though the sights of the martial world are wonderful, traveling alone inevitably brings memories of the lights back home. Realizing it has been a long time since I last wrote to you, and fearing you might worry, I took up my pen to send these greetings.
I encountered a delightful coincidence in Apricot Village recently. While passing through, I met someone with the exact same name as mine. He is also a Well of Heaven disciple and is acquainted with a wanderer who manages an Homestead. Upon further inquiry, I learned that the wanderer is named $C$L#Y$PN#E$C, and he is remarkably similar to you: a fellow traveler who cares for all living beings and fears no hardship.
Though the world is vast, such a coincidence is rare. I suppose only "destiny" can explain it.
While we were talking, I noticed that the other Shi Jingtian seemed troubled. It turns out his friend often climbs cliffs and braves dangers to seek secrets and treasures, frequently snagging his clothes. By the time his friend returns home, he is always in tattered rags and looks quite disheveled. The other Shi Jingtian wanted to go to Silken Veil Society in Kaifeng to learn sewing himself, but he was always delayed by chores.
Since we are fellow disciples, why fret over such a small matter? I decided to make the trip to Silken Veil Society for him to ask the seamstresses for some sewing tips. If I learn anything, I might be able to share your burdens in the future as well.
This will take some time. If I return late, please do not worry about me.
Shi Jingtian

zh:
但叶不休毕竟为他报仇了，王大演是个恩怨分明的好少年。因为道谢，他渐渐跟叶不休熟络起来，两人多了除了同窗和棋搭子以外的关系——朋友。
他知道他的冤种朋友成了今上的棋待诏，也知道他的冤种朋友深受今上喜爱——今上会在下棋时聊起自己曾经参加的战役，而叶不休，他的冤种朋友居然就此编出了一套用象棋演绎那些战役的棋谱，惹得龙颜大悦。而那套以棋演战之术，他看过，甚至尝试学过，却没有学会。他只能像一个呆呆的木偶，根据棋谱的指示行动，却无法理解为什么这一步出兵代表的是今上上源驿救太祖，而那一步出马就代表今上任城破梁军。
不都是今上吗？为什么一会儿是兵，一会儿是马？
“因为情势不同呗。”叶不休往嘴里扔了片橘子，轻飘飘地解释。
情势？什么是情势？又怎么看情势？不明白，真的不明白。王大演咬了咬腮帮子，止住心里不断往外冒的酸水儿。他不得不承认，天赋这种东西着实没什么道理，他与叶不休的差距也许比兵和车的战力差距还要大。但他并不打算就此放弃象棋，勤能补拙，他还有的是时间慢慢琢磨，总有一天，他得赢叶不休一局，然后将他狠狠教训一顿！
en:
But still, Ye Buxiu had stood up for him. Wang Dayan, knowing exactly who had helped him, gradually began to let his guard down. What started as a reluctant camaraderie between classmates and classmates soon deepened into genuine friendship.
Wang Dayan learned that his sparring friend had become the new Imperial Chess Attendant and earned the emperor's special favor. During their matches, the emperor would recount past battles, and Ye Buxiu cleverly turned those stories into a series of chess manuals that mirrored the campaigns. The emperor was thrilled. Wang Dayan read through the manuals and attempted to study them. But to him, the moves felt hollow, like the jerky motions of a puppet. He simply couldn't grasp the meaning behind them. 
Why did advancing a Soldier symbolize the emperor rescuing his foster father, the Grand Ancestor of the Later Tang? Why did moving a Horse signify defeating the Later Liang forces?
"Wait... it's still the same emperor, right? So why is His Majesty a Soldier in this move and a Horse in that one?"
"Depends on the situation," Ye Buxiu had replied vaguely, popping a wedge of orange into his mouth.
Situation? What situation? And how could you possibly grasp it? Wang Dayan was baffled, but he bit his tongue. He couldn't help but envy Ye Buxiu's instinctive talent. The gap between them was wider than the difference between a Soldier and a Chariot. But even so, he wasn't going to quit. He believed that with enough grit and persistence, one day he'd win a game and finally put Ye Buxiu in his place.

……

……

en:
A man already fallen to the ground cannot be struck down again. If one does not press forward, then hardship disperses of itself. Is this not a kind of invincibility?
... 
Lately I often feel alone, profoundly alone. Is the pursuit of learning truly such a lonely thing? If I do not befriend others, will they not come to befriend me? I may have my reasons for not seeking out my friends, but if my friends do not seek me out, then what are they waiting for?
...
Whenever I sit down to read and study, I suddenly feel the urge to drink water, relieve myself, or wash my hands. Only sitting still fails to please me. How very strange.
...
It rains heavily. Is it the rain that enfolds me, or I who enfold the rain? I would take my lady's hand, yet she draws back. Is it she who refuses me, or I who refuse her?

July 20
I failed the borrowing‑force technique again. But after my brother told me to attune myself to my five senses, I truly felt a small breakthrough.
August 15
Wonderful! Slow as I am, I managed to learn the first Tai Chi form within a month. No wonder my brother is highly valued!
September 1
My brother has created a move of his own atop the Tai Chi forms, which is even more powerful than anything before it. He really is a born genius.

My brother said #MTai Chi#E's softness can #Mbreak through the rigid strength of a shield#E. No sooner had he finished speaking than he #Mswept the shield straight from a bandit's grasp#E dozens of paces away. Amazing!

My brother's life is nothing like it used to be.
The mountain village of our childhood had its simple charms, but we lived in poverty, and the place was desolate and lonely.
At Inkbound Order, we were well taken care of, and the place had its own scholarly grace—but the strict rules made life feel stifling.

zh:
张淮深的刀法，是他叔父教的。
按照叔父的说法，刀法有三个境界——庸人用刀，异人听刀，至人无刀。
说的是刀客过招，庸碌的刀客只会粗浅的用刀。有异才的刀客，刀先到而声后至。而最擅用刀的刀客，他的刀从不出鞘，却已能败退所有敌人。
“可不出刀，又怎能退敌呢？”少年的张淮深，看着那个他所敬仰的叔父，不解疑问。
“因为所有人都认为，那柄不出刀的刀，便是世上最强的一刀。”
“世人大多对未知抱有敬畏，只要刀藏在鞘中，就存在着想象与顾忌。”
“可一旦出了鞘，所有人都见过它的样子，那柄刀便不复至人之刀。”
“但是……那柄刀出鞘的时候，所有人都翘首以盼，它也一定是最辉煌的一刀对不对？”
他的叔父一愣，看着眼前这个呆头呆脑的傻小子，有些感慨，沉吟片刻后才道：
“是，那会是最辉煌的一刀。”
张淮深忽然想着，或许叔父也曾和他一样，天不怕地不怕，少年意气，关山纵马。
他想了好久好久，想到叔父早就没了踪影。想到他忘记问叔父很多事——
可是现在，他再也没有那个问他的机会了。
他还在这里，他的叔父，却早已归唐。
漫长的岁月里，他的刀法越修越精湛，精湛到令人害怕，敌人惧怕它的威，朋党惧怕它的势。
这些畏惧汇聚到一起，便成了暗处的泥淖。
他忽又想起了那个至人之刀，恨不得出刀斩却泥淖，但是他不能出刀。
他蓦然明白，他这把刀，已经有了鞘。
鞘在长安，叔父就是他的鞘。
在那个至人无刀的故事里，是鞘保护了刀。但在他的故事里，刀却想保护鞘。
只要刀还在，鞘便还在。只要刀不断，鞘便不会亡。
他日复一日的奏请长安，将自己的锐气藏于鞘下。
他想保护的那个人，到底还是成了他的软肋。
昔日的傲骨，变为囚禁自我的监牢。
直到鞘归来凉州的那日。
那一天，全凉州的人都听到了刀的悲鸣。
那一瞬，人们见到了世上最辉煌的一刀。
此后无刀。
en:
Zhang Huaishen's swordsmanship was taught by his uncle. 
According to his uncle, swordsmanship has three realms, mediocre men wield swords, extraordinary men listen to swords, and supreme men need no swords. 
It means in a duel, mediocre swordsmen only use their blades crudely. Extraordinary ones strike before the sound of the sword reaches the enemy. The greatest swordsman, however, never draws his sword, yet he can repel all foes. 
"But how can you repel enemies without drawing your sword?" The young Zhang Huaishen looked at his revered uncle, confused. 
"Because everyone believes that the sword that remains sheathed is the strongest in the world." 
"Most people hold awe for the unknown. As long as the sword stays in its sheath, imagination and hesitation linger in their minds." 
"But once drawn, everyone sees its true form, and it is no longer the sword of a supreme man." 
"But... when that sword is drawn, everyone waits eagerly. It must be the most brilliant strike, right?" 
His uncle froze, looking at the naive boy in front of him, filled with emotion. After a moment of hesitation, he said, 
"Yes. It will be the most brilliant strike." 
Zhang Huaishen suddenly thought that perhaps his uncle was once like him, fearless, youthful, riding freely across mountains and rivers. 
He thought for a long, long time, until he remembered his uncle had long since disappeared. He realized he had forgotten to ask him so many things... 
But now, he would never get the chance to ask. 
He was still here, but his uncle had already returned to the Tang. 
Over the long years, his swordsmanship became increasingly exquisite, so exquisite it inspired fear. Enemies feared its power and allies feared its influence. 
All these fears merged into a quagmire in the shadows. 
He suddenly recalled the "supreme man's sword," longing to draw his own and slash through the quagmire, but he couldn't. 
Suddenly, he understood that his sword already had a sheath. 
The sheath was in Chang'an, his uncle was his sheath. 
In the story of the supreme man without a sword, the sheath protects the blade. But in his story, the blade wanted to protect the sheath. 
As long as the blade exists, the sheath exists. As long as the blade remains unbroken, the sheath will not perish. 
Day after day, he petitioned Chang'an, hiding his sharpness beneath the sheath. 
The person he wanted to protect had ultimately become his weakness. 
His former pride had turned into a prison confining himself. 
Until the day the sheath returned to Liangzhou. 
On that day, everyone in Liangzhou heard the sword's lament. 
In that moment, people witnessed the most brilliant strike in the world. 
After that, there was no sword left.

zh:
叶片在火光前盘旋，渐渐汇聚成一个人的身影。那面容看不真切，只听见四周人群将那人称为了“侠”。
一阵风来，火更大了一些。弥漫的灰烟里，那个身影似乎不再是一片片零落之叶。
那是将满江红洒向地面的酒痕吗？一壶好酒，祭未能及此的英魂，祭尚未可卜的明日，祭并肩杀虏的承诺。
那是夜里雪落肩头的剪影吗？一把陌刀，自雪山中来，向血海中去。在他的身后，三百弟子，秉义而来。
那是母亲遥指着的那片云吗？一封别信，敛去了未说完的话，等着归乡的一日，再亲口告诉她的孩子。
那是军帐中那盏彻夜晃动的烛火吗？一身戎装，用一道道军令，一封封信札，铺就粮车缓缓前行的路途。
风再吹过，万千叶影零落空中。驻足倾听之人，可听到了，它们与风一同讲述的故事？
en:
The leaves circle before the firelight, slowly gathering into the shape of a single figure. The face cannot be made out clearly; one only hears the crowd around it calling that figure a "hero."
A gust of wind, and the fire rises higher. In the drifting gray smoke, the figure seems no longer a scatter of falling leaves.
Is that the wine stain of a River All Red poured out upon the ground? A flask of good wine, offered to the heroic souls who could not make it this far, to a tomorrow no one can foretell, to a vow to slay the invaders side by side.
Is that the silhouette of night snow settling on a shoulder? A Mo blade, come down from the snowbound peaks and bound for a sea of blood, and behind it three hundred disciples, come in the name of righteousness.
Is that the cloud a mother once pointed toward? A parting letter, folding away all the words left unspoken, waiting for the day of homecoming to tell them to her child in person.
Is that the candle that swayed all night long in the war tent? A suit of armor, paving the slow road forward for the grain carts, order by order, letter by letter.
The wind blows again, and thousands of leaf-shadows scatter through the air. You who pause and listen, have you heard the story they tell together with the wind?

zh:
……
天复元年，韩全海挟天子前往凤翔投岐王，宫廷大乱。
师父言道，覆巢之下无完卵，我们只好离了长安。
那时我已二十出头，仍未发身长大，师父却已早生华发，如同老者。同路出逃的人只当我与师父为爷孙，殊不知他的年纪做我父亲尤嫌小了几岁。
……
托鹿公鹿婆的福，我们在渭阳屯有了落脚之地。师父喜欢此地民风淳朴，我们便留下结庐行医。
可叹师父一身医术，救了无数百姓，却没能救得自己。若我能学到他五分医术，或许还能……
……
师父走了，我只剩下自己。可这样的残疾之躯，迟早会被发觉。年月更迭，三年、五年尚且不怕，十年、二十年又当如何？
一个几十年都外貌如女童的郎中，在世人眼里究竟是人，还是妖怪？
我所中的毒没有要了我的命，却也让我生不如死。
……
我修改了师父留下的吐纳之法，似乎在月夜更为有效。但也只能暂缓毒性罢了。
近日我收留了一个孩子，她有些像我，更像师父。若我毒发不治，有她在，师父的医术也不至于失了传承。
……
en:
...
In the first year of the Tianfu era, Han Quanhai took the emperor to Fengxiang to seek refuge with Prince Qi, throwing the palace into chaos.
My master said, "When the nest falls, no egg stays whole." So we had no choice but to flee Chang'an.
I was already in my twenties then, still wet behind the ears. My master was already white-headed, aged beyond his years. Folks we met on the road assumed we were grandfather and grandson, never knowing he was years younger than my father would have been.
...
Thanks to Lord and Madam Lu's kindness, we settled in Weiyang Village. My master liked the honest folk there, so we built a hut and practiced medicine. It is a cruel irony that my master, who saved thousands, could not save himself. If only I had learned even a fraction of what he knew... maybe I could have...
...
Now my master's gone, and I'm alone. But people will notice my abnormalities sooner or later.
A doctor who remains a child for decades, in the eyes of the world, would I be seen as a human or a monster?
The poison inside me hasn't killed me yet, but it makes living unbearable.
...
I've adapted my master's breathing methods. They work better under moonlight, but they only slow the poison, nothing more.
I took in a child recently. She reminds me of myself, and even more, she reminds me of my master. If the poison takes me, at least she can carry forward his legacy.
...
Falling into the Well

zh:
游侠，我的研究生涯怕是要到头了。唉，这人若是倒霉，当真连喝凉水都塞牙缝。
前几日有位乡亲寻到我，说自己失眠脱发，问我可有什么巧法子。他不愿用髢髦，一定要从根上治起。我见他言辞恳切，便动了心，为他翻遍古籍，外敷内服，什么法子都试了……可是今早他一进门，我就觉得屋里格外亮堂——他那本就稀疏的头顶，竟比前日更空旷了！
我还没理清是哪儿出了问题，他就抡起袖子，抄着扫帚，追着我满街跑，边跑边说要告到墨山道去，把我开除，然后拉着我一起剃度出家当和尚，街坊们全都探头看热闹……
游侠，你说说，我这本是热心帮忙，怎么反倒成了灭顶之灾了……
en:
Wanderer, I'm afraid my research career may be over. When your luck turns, even a sip of cold water seems to catch in your teeth.
A few days ago, one of the villagers came to me complaining of insomnia and hair loss, asking if I had any clever remedies. He refused to wear a hairpiece, insisting on fixing the problem at the root. He sounded so sincere that I took pity on him. I scoured ancient texts for him, trying everything from topical ointments to internal remedies... But this morning, the second he walked through the door, I felt the room suddenly get much brighter. His scalp, already sparse to begin with, was even barer than the day before!
Before I could figure out what had gone wrong, he rolled up his sleeves, grabbed a broom, and chased me halfway across town. The whole time he was yelling that he'd report me to Mohist Hill, get me expelled, and then drag me off to have my head shaved and become a monk with him. The neighbors all came out to watch the commotion...
Wanderer, how did trying to help turn into such a catastrophe?

zh:
狗界传闻，城里有些武功高强的贼，能悄无声息地偷走宝贝。
这可把大耳朵吓得够呛，因为它恰好有个天大的宝贝——大棒骨。
以前没什么吃的，大耳朵饿得只剩皮包骨，一对耳朵比脸还大。路过的女人给它扔了根大棒骨，它哼哧哼哧地把骨头舔得干干净净，还不肯丢呢，走到哪儿带到哪儿，这根大棒骨是它最爱的狗宝贝，是天底下最完美的骨头。
大耳朵觉得，就这根骨头，没人看了不想舔一口，这种稀世珍宝，一旦被发现了，大盗能忍得住？
大耳朵不敢细想，叼着宝贝跟着叮当找到了金水门街的老大——大聪明。
三个狗脑袋凑到一块儿，一场狗狗大会开始了。
大聪明很是烦恼，因为它把自己的宝贝——布老虎在各处墙角埋了挖、挖了又埋。布老虎上小主人的味道越来越淡了，只剩些土腥气。
而叮当呢？连走路都缩着狗脑袋，蹑手蹑脚，生怕这宝贝铃铛清脆的声音把大盗们招来。
怎么办？怎么办？怎么办？
三只狗你冲着我，我冲着你汪了好几圈儿，它们呀是真没招了。
en:
Rumor has it among dogs that there are martial arts masters among the thieves, capable of stealing treasures without a sound.
This terrifies Big Ears because he happens to have a huge treasure, a giant meaty bone.
Back when there was little to eat, Big Ears was skin and bones, his ears bigger than his face. A passing woman threw him this bone. He licked it clean, then refused to let it go. He carries it everywhere. This bone is his most beloved treasure, the perfect bone in all the world.
Big Ears figures anyone who sees this bone will want a lick. Such a rare treasure, once discovered, how could any thief resist?
Big Ears doesn't dare think about it. He grabs his treasure and follows Jingle to find the boss of Goldwater Street, Big Smart.
Three dog heads huddle together. A doggy summit commences.
Big Smart is troubled: he has been burying and digging up his cloth tiger in various corners. The scent of his young owner fades more each day, leaving only earthiness.
And Jingle? He creeps around with his head down, terrified that his precious bell's clear jingling will attract the thieves.
What to do? What to do? WHAT TO DO?
The three dogs woof at each other in circles. They really, truly have no idea.

zh:
两年四十二天，我晒了很多药，也治好了很多人。直到你和狐令飞约战的消息传来。
我忽然发现，我还是很想你，很担心你。
想着也许……你会需要我呢。
等回过神来，信已经写到了这里。人也已经在路上了。
我能去见你吗？如果见到你，你会和我说话吗？如果见到你，我能和你说话吗？
如果我们说话，又会说什么呢？
也许什么都不说。就只是像第一次交换名字时那样，两个人静静地看着冰面，看了许久，小小的你忽然抽出剑来，一剑划过
凌冽的冰上，腾起一尾尾鲜活的鱼，你回头看我，鼻尖红红的，轻声问，请你吃鱼，要么？
我始终很乐意的。
en:
Two years and forty-two days have passed. I've dried many herbs and healed many people. Then, word of your duel with Hu Lingfei reached me.
And suddenly I realized, I still miss you. I still worry about you. I thought, maybe... you might need me.
Before I knew it, I had already written this much. And I was already on my way.
Can I come see you? If I do, will you speak to me? If I do, can I speak to you?
And if we do speak, what would we even say?
Perhaps nothing at all. Just like the first time we exchanged names. Just the two of us, gazing quietly at the frozen lake, for a long time. Then, you will suddenly draw your sword, and with a single slash...
...pull a lively fish from the icy water. You'll turn to look at me, your nose red from the cold, and ask softly, "Would you like some fish?"
I would, Yuzhen. And I always will.

失刺孙，与猞猁狲、失利、实鲁苏、宿列荪、沙鲁思、舍列孙、失剌孙、舍里孙、扯里狲等，均曾为古人对猞猁这一小型猛兽的称呼。它们多经丝绸之路，从西域各国带入唐朝宫廷，作为贡品进献。
外形上，猞猁看起来像猫，但比猫体型更大、躯干更粗壮、四肢更长，尾巴较短，耳朵尖而有毛簇，也更为凶猛。因此，唐代贵族常驯养猞猁作为打猎的帮手。
但现存的考古证据和古籍记录还不能完全确认唐朝人所养的猞猁就是今日所说的猞猁，也不能确定它们与现代猞猁是否同一物种。
en:
Shilasun, along with names such as Shalishun, Shili, Shilusu, Suliesun, Shalusi, Sheliesun, Shilason, Shelisun, and Chelisun, was one of several terms used in antiquity to refer to the lynx, a small predatory beast. These animals were often brought along the Silk Road from the Western Regions and presented to the Tang court as tribute.
In appearance, the lynx resembles a cat, but is larger, with a sturdier build, longer limbs, a shorter tail, and pointed ears tipped with tufts of fur. It is also notably more ferocious. For this reason, Tang aristocrats frequently kept lynxes as hunting companions.
However, existing archaeological evidence and historical records cannot fully confirm that the animals kept during the Tang dynasty were the same as the lynx known today, nor whether they belonged to the same species as modern lynxes.

Since parting ways at Jadestream Valley, you have frequently received letters from the Three Junior Paragons of Mohist City.
"Great Wanderer, why haven't you come to play with us yet?"
"Great Wanderer! How's the Sky Shuttle in the mountains coming along? When can you take us for another ride?"
But above all, they pester about Master Raven's "seeds."
"Where on earth are the seeds?"
"Have the seeds grown up yet?"
"Are the seeds doing well?"
...
You sit down to write back:
#Y[The seeds have grown plump.] Have the three of you been eating well? It's been a while since we last met; I'll surely visit you when I have the time.#E
After sending the letter, you visit Mohist City. You pick up the long-awaiting children and board the Sky Shuttle once more, gliding along the completed tracks back to Jadestream Valley.
The seeds are in the golden rice paddies, amidst the falling petals of Peach Grove, and within the gurgling brooks... The seeds are growing very, very well.

zh: “玄衣缀金玉，额间悬双星。”乌金长得标致，身姿也是小狗里数一数二的那类，每日精神抖擞地巡视一圈被人叫做都城驿的大房子，便能收获许多摸摸和夸赞。摸摸，乌金明白，是人喜欢乌金。叽里咕噜，乌金不明白，人都在说什么？每每那些穿得花花绿绿、金光闪闪的人蹲下来和乌金打招呼，乌金就摇摇尾巴，坐下来、歪着头、认真听——听不懂。小狗儿鼻子灵光，能闻得出来面前这栋大房子里每个人身上的不同气味，有的人身上有浓浓的香料味道，有的人身上有咸咸的潮湿味道，有的人身上有冷冷的北风味道……小狗乌金身上也有味道，是青石板路边青苔的味道，是傍晚厨房柴火的味道，是雨后粘在爪子上的泥土的味道，是家的味道。乌金每天都能回家，所以身上的味道一直都浓浓的，但大房子里的人，他们身上家的味道会越来越淡、越来越淡。乌金歪头看向他们，人啊，会不会找不到回家的路呢？
en: "A coat of ebon black, adorned with gold and jade; twin stars shining upon his brow." Black Gold is a handsome dog, and one of the finest built you'll find. Each day he makes brisk rounds through the great house folks call the Capital Relay, and comes away with no small share of pets and praise. Petting—this much Black Gold knows—means the people are fond of him. But the babble of words, Black Gold doesn't understand. What are they all saying? Whenever the people in bright colors and shining gold crouch down to greet him, Black Gold wags his tail, sits down, tilts his head, and listens intently, but he understands not a word. A dog's nose is keen, and Black Gold can smell the different scents on everyone in that big house. Some carry the heavy perfume of spices, some the salty dampness of the sea, some the cold of the north wind... Black Gold, too, carries his own scent. The smell of moss along the bluestone path, firewood smoke from the kitchen at dusk, mud clinging to his paws after the rain—the smell of home. Black Gold goes home every day, so his scent always stays strong. But for the people in that big house, the smell of home on them grows fainter, and fainter still. Black Gold tilts his head and looks at them. Would these people, he wonders, lose their way home?

【竹木】

松
李峤
郁郁高岩表，森森幽涧陲。

百尺条阴合，千年盖影披。

en:
【Bamboo & Wood】

【Bamboo】

Bamboo Lodge
Wang Wei
Alone I sit in bamboo grove so dense,
Playing the lute and whistling at my ease.
None knows the depth of woods where I'm so dense,
But the bright moon comes to shine on me.

Bamboo of Mother Stone
Li Bai
Wild bamboos grow from rocks in clusters tight,
Veiled in mist, they're mirrored in isles' stream.
Their green reflection deepens water's light;
Their hollow sound announces cold, it seems.
I've never heard the dragon's song so fine,
But phoenix's tune on them would sound divine.
They won't, like willows, wither in decline,
Their faithful hearts will keep their verdure prime.

In Reply to Attendant Censor Lu's Ode to Bamboo
Zhang Jiuling
Pure and fresh, they hang o'er purple hall,
Luxuriant, their dewy leaves are spread.
Their color won't change with the moon at all;
Their sound is wafted by the wind, instead.
Their lofty joints by people are esteemed;
Their hollow hearts are known to all, it's deemed.
Good food for phoenix, they may be esteemed,
Coming and going, they're a ritual theme.

【Pine】

The Pine
Li Qiao
Luxuriant, it towers o'er the height,
Dense, it stands by the deep ravine's dark side.
Cranes perch on branches of the tree of right;
The wind caresses twigs with lordly pride.
Its shade of hundred feet in union lies;
Its cover of a thousand years outspreads.
It won't change in cold years 'neath wintry skies;
Its sturdy joints are known to you, it's said.

The Lone Pine by Southern Verandah
Li Bai
By southern verandah a lone pine stands,
Its branches and leaves spread in dense array.
The fresh breeze blows on it with tireless hands,
Carefree, it stands there from night until day.
In its shade ancient moss grows thick and green,
Its color dyed by autumn mist so blue.
When will it tower into clouds unseen,
Soaring up thousands of feet into view?

Asking Magistrate Wei Ban for a Pine Sapling
Du Fu
Alone it towers, not like elms or willows;
Evergreen, can it be like waxberries?
To keep the old tree's meaning through long years,
I seek a sapling with frosty root, please.

On an Ancient Pine in Liugou Temple
Bai Juyi
Its misty leaves like dark deer's tail appear;
Its mottled bark looks like purple dragon's scale.
To know how old the pine is, look at the wall,
And see how many poets wrote in vain.

【Willow】

Ode to the Willow
He Zhizhang
The slender tree is dressed in emerald all about;
A thousand branches droop like fringes made of jade.
But do you know by whom these slim leaves are cut out?
The wind of early spring is sharp as scissor blade.

Written on Riverside Willows
Yu Xuanji
Their verdure spreads along the rivershore;
Their mist-veiled forms stretch into towers far.
Their shadows fall on autumn water's floor;
Their falling blooms on angler's head appear.
Their old roots hide the fish in deep retreat;
Their low twigs fasten boats of parting guest.
In dreary wind and rain on sad night fleet,
They wake from dreams and aggravate unrest.

The New Willow
Du Mu
Too weak to wave in wind at dawn so new,
Her slender waist envied by beauties fair.
Her green shade not yet covering long dike's view,
Her golden catkins welcome spring in garden rare.
In several places, hearts break for long way;
A twig with rain sees off the dust of part.
Outside the east gate, partings sadden the day,
And kill with grief the people, heart to heart.

【All Grasses】

A Spring View
Du Fu
On war-torn land streams flow and mountains stand;
In vernal town grass and weeds are o'er-grown.
Grieved o'er the years, flowers make us shed tears;
Hating to part, hearing birds breaks our heart.
The beacon fire has gone higher and higher;
Words from household are worth their weight in gold.
I cannot bear to scratch my grizzling hair;
It grows too thin to hold a light hairpin.

Early Spring: To Secretary Zhang
Han Yu
The royal streets are moistened by a creamlike rain;
Green grass can be perceived afar but not nearby.
It's the best time of a year you try in vain
To find a view better than where willows run high.

Grass on the Ancient Plain - Farewell to a Friend
Bai Juyi
Wild grasses spread o'er ancient plain;
With spring and fall they come and go.
Wild fire can't burn them up, again
They rise when vernal breezes blow.
Their fragrance overruns the way;
Their green invades the ruined town.
To see my friend go far away,
My sorrow grows like grass o'ergrown.

zh: 马乳制成的干酪酥虽然坚硬，但适宜保存。唐代盛行食用乳酪，也就是牛羊马等动物的乳汁加工而成的稠状奶制品，将乳酪进一步煎炼，便可得到酥和醍醐。白居易《晚起》诗中云：“融雪煎香茗，调酥煮乳糜”，描绘的就是煎茶煮酪酥的景象。
en: Dry Sweet Curd, made from mare's milk is notably hard but well suited for long-term storage. In the Tang Dynasty, people widely consumed fermented dairy products such as cheese, which was thickened from the milk of cows, sheep, or horses. With further refinement, these products were transformed into two distinct forms: curd and the finest essence. The poet Bai Juyi described this culinary craft in his poem Rising Late. He wrote, "With melted snow, I brew fragrant tea; seasoned with curds I cook a milk pudding." These lines offer a vivid glimpse into the custom of brewing tea and drying sweet curd.

zh: 北宋后宫制度在宋徽宗时期定型为五等：正一品（贵妃、淑妃、德妃、贤妃）、正二品（嫔，如昭仪、昭容等）、正三品（婕妤）、正四品（美人）、正五品（才人）。贵妃位列“四妃”之首，是仅次于皇后的高级封号（皇后不列品级）。选项中的“从一品”在北宋后宫体系中并未设立，常见误区是混淆了唐代制度。
en: During the reign of Emperor Huizong of Song, the harem system was standardized into five ranks: First Rank (Noble Consort, Pure Consort, Virtuous Consort, Able Consort), Second Rank (Concubine, e.g., Lady of Bright Deportment, Lady of Bright Countenance), Third Rank (Lady of Handsome Fairness), Fourth Rank (Lady of Beauty), Fifth Rank (Lady of Talent). Noble Consort ranks first among the "Four Consorts" and is second only to the Empress (who is outside the ranking system). The option "Subsidiary First Rank" does not exist in the Northern Song harem system; this is a common confusion with the Tang dynasty system.

zh:
【月令第六】

孟春之月，日在营室，昏参中，旦尾中。其日甲乙。其帝大皞，其神句芒。其虫鳞。其音角，律中大蔟。其数八。其味酸，其臭膻。其祀户，祭先脾。
东风解冻，蛰虫始振，鱼上冰，獭祭鱼，鸿雁来。
天子居青阳左个，乘鸾路，驾仓龙，载青旗，衣青衣，服仓玉，食麦与羊，其器疏以达。
是月也，以立春。先立春三日，大史谒之天子曰：某日立春，盛德在木。天子乃齐。
立春之日，天子亲帅三公、九卿、诸侯、大夫以迎春于东郊。还反，赏公卿、诸侯、大夫于朝。
命相布德和令，行庆施惠，下及兆民，庆赐遂行，毋有不当。
乃命大史，守典奉法，司天日月星辰之行，宿离不贷，毋失经纪，以初为常。
是月也，天子乃以元日祈榖于上帝。乃择元辰，天子亲载耒耜，措之于参保介之御间，帅三公、九卿、诸侯、大夫躬耕帝籍。天子三推，三公五推，卿、诸侯九推。反，执爵于大寝，三公、九卿、诸侯、大夫皆御，命曰劳酒。
是月也，天气下降，地气上腾，天地和同，草木萌动。王命布农事，命田舍东郊，皆修封疆，审端经术，善相丘陵、阪险、原隰土地所宜，五榖所殖，以教道民，必躬亲之。田事既饬，先定准直，农乃不惑。
是月也，命乐正入学习舞，乃修祭典，命祀山林川泽，牺牲母用牝。
禁止伐木。母覆巢，母杀孩虫，胎天飞鸟，母麛，母卵。母聚大众，母置城郭，掩骼埋瘠。
是月也，不可以称兵，称兵必天殃，兵戎不起，不可从我始。毋变天之道，毋绝地之理，毋乱人之纪。
孟春行夏令，则雨水不时肥，草木蚤落，国时有恐。行秋令，则民大疫，猋风暴雨总至，藜莠蓬蒿并兴。行冬令，则水潦为败，雪霜大挚，首种不入。
……

【Monthly Ordinance VI】

In the first month of spring, the sun is in the constellation of Yingshi; at dusk, the constellation Shen culminates, and at dawn, the constellation Wei culminates. Its days are Jia and Yi. Its sovereign is Taihao, and its deity is Gou Mang. Its creatures are the scaly ones. Its sound is Jue, and its pitch is Dazhong. Its number is eight. Its flavor is sour, and its odor is rank. Its sacrifice is to the door, and the offering is placed before the spleen.
The east wind thaws the frozen ground, hibernating insects begin to stir, fish rise to the ice, otters offer fish in sacrifice, and wild geese arrive.
The Emperor resides in the left chamber of the Azure Resolve, rides in the phoenix chariot, harnesses the azure dragon, flies the azure banner, wears azure robes, and carries azure jade. He eats wheat and mutton, and his vessels are sparse and penetrating.
In this month, the beginning of spring is established. Three days before the beginning of spring, the Grand Astrologer announces to the Emperor: "On such-and-such a day, spring begins, and the virtue of Wood prevails." The Emperor then fasts.
On the day of the beginning of spring, the Emperor personally leads the Three Dukes, Nine Ministers, feudal lords, and Doctors to welcome spring at the eastern suburb. Upon returning, he rewards the Dukes, Ministers, feudal lords, and Doctors at court.
He orders the Prime Minister to spread virtue and harmonize ordinances, to dispense celebrations and bestow kindness, reaching down to the myriad people. Celebrations and rewards proceed without any impropriety.
He then orders the Grand Astrologer to uphold the statutes and observe the laws, to oversee the movements of heaven, sun, moon, and stars, so that their positions and conjunctions are without error, and nothing violates the celestial order, taking the beginning as the constant.
In this month, the Emperor, on the first auspicious day, prays to the Supreme Deity for a good harvest. He then selects an auspicious hour, personally carries the plow and share, places them between the guards of his chariot, and leads the Three Dukes, Nine Ministers, feudal lords, and Doctors to personally till the Emperor's field. The Emperor pushes three times, the Three Dukes five times, and the Ministers and feudal lords nine times. Upon returning, he holds a cup in the grand chamber, with the Three Dukes, Nine Ministers, feudal lords, and Doctors all in attendance, and it is called the Wine of Labor.
In this month, the weather descends, the earth's vapor rises, heaven and earth are in harmony, and grasses and trees begin to sprout. The King orders the dissemination of farming affairs, commands the field officers to lodge in the eastern suburbs, and all to repair the boundaries and embankments, to carefully survey the hills, slopes, dangerous heights, plains, and lowlands, determining what the land is suitable for, and what the five grains can be planted in, in order to instruct and guide the people, and he must personally attend to it. Once the farming affairs are arranged, standards and measures are first fixed, and the farmers will not be confused.
In this month, the Stage Director is ordered to enter the school and practice dances, and to revise the sacrificial statutes. He is ordered to perform sacrifices to mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes, and the victims must not be female.
Chopping wood is forbidden. Do not overturn nests, do not kill young insects, do not harm creatures in the womb or flying birds in the egg, do not take fawns, and do not take eggs. Do not gather great multitudes, do not build walls and fortifications, and cover exposed bones and bury the dead.
In this month, one must not raise arms; if arms are raised, calamity will surely follow. Military actions must not arise, and cannot be initiated by us. Do not alter the ways of heaven, do not sever the principles of earth, and do not disturb the order of man.
If the ordinances of summer are carried out in the first month of spring, then rain will fall unseasonably, grasses and trees will wither early, and the state will be frequently alarmed. If the ordinances of autumn are carried out, then the people will suffer great pestilence, whirlwinds and torrential rains will arrive together, and weeds and brambles will flourish side by side. If the ordinances of winter are carried out, then floods will cause ruin, frost and snow will fall heavily, and the first sowings will not enter the ground.

横在店门前，浑身没一块好皮，肉翻出来，往外渗血。
这样的人在这一片并不稀奇，总会被扔出来几个，有时候挡了东家的店，有时候挡了西家的店，今儿算我们倒霉，被这团烂肉挡我们店前了。
掌柜去处理这晦气事，没成想她还有力气龇着牙，低吼着不让近身，掌柜踢这团烂肉的脚，被一锭银子挡住了。

春姑娘用一锭银子买下了这团烂肉，烂肉是走不了的，所以姑娘将她抱回屋，衣摆染了血，银子也染了血。
这是极不值当的买卖。烂肉不值得弄脏银子，也不值得弄脏衣服，可姑娘不觉得。
她什么都不懂，姑娘教她穿衣，教她走路，教她认字。
她不见了，姑娘就一个院一个院地敲门，把那些男人们都吓得提上裤子。
她总在天黑才回来，伤都没好全的人，捧着一束白花，那是我们都没见过的便宜货。
可偏生每一次，姑娘接过花就笑。

她这一待，就是一个春天。
这个春天长，长到院里的迎春花开了又谢，店里的账清了又结，长到话都说不囫囵的人，也能断续念出几个词。
听说，她学会说的第一个字，是“春”。
这事我不知真假，我只知道，她跟我说的第一个字，是“钱”。
看来在这做生意的地方待久了，她也知道什么能买了。
她问我，买一个春天，要多少钱。
en:
I'm just a waiter. Working here, you see all kinds of things. This is a place where anything can be bought—a dog, a person, or, for the right price, a person turned into a dog.
But the strangest deal I ever saw began the day a body lay at our doorstep. It looked more beast than human, torn and bleeding. Around here, that's nothing new—just our turn to clean up the mess. 
The boss went to kick it aside, but it bared its teeth, and a silver ingot rolled to his feet. Miss Chun bought that body with that piece of silver. She carried the girl herself, blood soaking her clothes and coins. 
A poor bargain, but Miss Chun didn't care. She taught the girl to walk, to read, to live. When the girl vanished, Miss Chun went door to door, banging on gates, scaring half-dressed men out of their wits. The girl always returned after dark with a bunch of cheap white flowers in hand.
She stayed one long spring—long enough for forsythia to bloom and wither, long enough for the girl to speak. They say her first word was "Chun (spring)." But to me, it was "money." 
"How much," she asked, "to buy spring?"

zh:
时间过得真快，眨眼此时便成为前尘。范撒也未曾料到，自己用边角料做馒头的事会被注意到。
官家看不得浪费粮食，尚食局便想到了范撒和她的边角料馒头，羊骨头上残留的羊肉和陈年面粉生而逢时，哪怕是边角料，她也细细切好，慢慢调味，如同对待自己生命里每个重要时刻。
范撒在尚食局的边角处支起摊子，有人驻足，走走停停，从各个边角处来的足迹遍布了整个皇宫。
她嘴笨，面对每个买了馒头的人，其实有一箩筐的问题问不出。譬如是否合口味？是否要换些花样？宫人大多来去匆匆，她只来得及说一句，再忙也要好好吃饭。
说得多了，范撒便在这句话里找到了自己，她惊觉原来这就是好日子，无需做成什么大事，只要好好吃饭就好。
en:
Time flew. She never expected anyone to notice her habit of rescuing scraps.
The Culinary Office, strict about waste since the Emperor could not bear to see food wasted, did notice. Bits of lamb clinging to a bone, old flour, anything that could be saved found its way into her hands. She treated each fragment with care, slicing and seasoning them as deliberately as if tending a memory.
They gave her a stall in a quiet corner in the Culinary Office. People began to pause, then to return. Footsteps from all parts of the palace came to her counter.
She was shy with words and could never ask her customers everything she wanted to know. Did they like it? Want something different? So the one thing she always managed to call after them was simple: "No matter how busy you are, eat well."
Saying that so often, she realized it contained everything she'd been searching for. The "good life" was not a fortune or a title. It was this: making honest food and making sure people ate it. That, she discovered, was enough.

While the blossoms sleep in quiet grace, the wind whispers with yearning. Rumors swirl like autumn leaves around the performer of the Masked Troupe, igniting endless whispers in hushed corners.
